Job Description:
The Department of Media Production, Management, and Technology (MPMT) in the University of Florida's College of Journalism and Communications seeks to hire a tenure-track Assistant Professor with a demonstrated record of creative production to begin Fall 2027.
We seek a dynamic scholar/practitioner whose creative output advances storytelling through innovative media formats. We value candidates who push boundaries in media innovation and foster content that addresses contemporary social issues, cultural narratives, or technological disruptions.
The ideal candidate will demonstrate excellence in creative production while maintaining industry connections. Areas of expertise may include feature-length and short films, television series and specials, documentary filmmaking, emerging technologies such as augmented reality (AR) or virtual reality (VR), streaming series development and production, or hybrid formats that blend narrative with interactive elements. This role emphasizes a robust portfolio of creative work—such as films, documentaries, series, or interactive projects—alongside teaching and service contributions.
The MPMT department recognizes the critical importance of creative tenure tracks where artistic output is valued as highly as traditional scholarly research. Tenure evaluation will prioritize impactful creative scholarship, evidenced by honors and awards at nationally recognized film festivals, publications in creative outlets, peer-reviewed exhibitions, grants from bodies like the National Endowment for the Arts, or collaborations with industry leaders.
Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate courses in media production (for example, filmmaking techniques; camera and lens systems; documentary storytelling; VR/AR production; streaming content creation; mentoring students in hands-on projects; supervising capstone productions) and integrating emerging technologies into the curriculum. Candidates are expected to maintain an active agenda of original creative work, secure external funding, and disseminate outputs through festivals, broadcasts, online platforms, or academic conferences. Service duties include department and college committees, advising student media organizations, and contributing to college initiatives and other duties as assigned.

The Department of Media Production, Management, and Technology is one of the premier programs in offering courses related to mass media and emerging media. Our curriculum prepares students for the media industry through two specializations: Digital Film and Video Production, and Media Management and Technology. The department has about 500 student majors and 16 full-time faculty. Students from the department pursue careers in film production, TV program production, social media management, brand management, consumer analysis, UI/UX design, and digital marketing, among others. Media Production, Management, and Technology (MPMT) - UF College of Journalism and Communications

We are recognized as a national leader in communication scholarship and professional skills development. Be part of an ambitious, progressive, and collaborative program at one of the top public research universities in the United States.

With over 70 full-time faculty members and 175 part- time instructors serving in four academic departments— Advertising; Journalism; Media Production, Management, and Technology; and Public Relations —we enroll about 2,500 undergraduates both in-person and online. Additionally, more than 700 graduate students are earning master's and doctoral degrees.
The College of Journalism and Communications offers multiple research and teaching environments, including the Atlas Lab for social media listening; the Consortium on Trust in Media and Technology; the STEM Translational Communication Center; the Center for Public Interest Communications; the Media, Effects, and Technology Lab; the Institute for Public Relations; The Agency, a full- service student-run advertising and public relations agency; the Innovation News Center; Division of Media Properties; and more. he University of Florida is situated in north-central Florida, a region renowned for its abundant natural beauty. Gainesville is within a two-hour drive of Tampa, Orlando, Jacksonville, the Atlantic Ocean, and the Gulf of Mexico.

As home to Florida's largest and oldest university, Gainesville (http://cityofgainesville.org (http://cityofgainesville.org/)) is one of the state's centers of education, medicine, cultural events, and athletics. Endowed Chair and Executive Director, Anita Zucker Center for Excellence in Early Childhood Studies
Job No: 537859

Classification Minimum Requirements:
A candidate for Associate Professor shall hold the highest degree appropriate to their field or possess professional qualifications above those equivalent to the highest degree relevant to their field. They are expected to have produced creative work, professional writing, or research and successful teaching or professional experience. A candidate for this rank must have a distinguished record of achievement beyond the assistant professor level.
A candidate for Professor shall be qualified for the rank of associate professor and, in addition, be a recognized national or international authority or an outstanding teacher in their field or specialization. A candidate for this rank must have a distinguished record of achievement beyond the associate professor level.
Job Description:
The University of Florida seeks applications for the David Lawrence Jr. Endowed Chair in Early Childhood Studies, a 12-month tenure-track associate or full professor appointment. The Endowed Chair will also hold an administrative appointment as the Executive Director of the Anita Zucker Center for Excellence in Early Childhood Studies. These roles recognize an eminent scholar with a national or international reputation for research, policy leadership, and transformative initiatives in child development, and early childhood studies or education. The Director and Chair will provide visionary leadership to advance transdisciplinary research, policy, and practice that supports the development, well-being, learning, and optimal outcomes for young children and their families.
The David Lawrence, Jr. Endowed Chair in Early Childhood Studies will have a faculty appointment in an academic unit (e.g., the School of Special Education, School Psychology, and Early Childhood Studies). The Endowed Chair will also hold an administrative appointment as the Executive Director of the Anita Zucker Center for Excellence in Early Childhood Studies. The Center endowment serves as a robust reserve and resource for advancing the Center's initiatives and the financially-sound Lawrence endowment will support the Chair holder's own research activities.
Key Responsibilities:
Strategic Leadership: Provide vision and leadership as the Director for the Anita Zucker Center and Endowed Chair in Early Childhood Studies, advancing transdisciplinary research and policy initiatives in early childhood.
Research and Scholarship: Conduct high-quality, impactful research in early childhood studies and maintain a strong record of scholarly publications.
Policy Engagement: Play a prominent role in national and international discussions on early childhood policy, advocating for optimal outcomes for all young children, their families, and the practitioners that support them
Collaboration and Outreach: Strengthen partnerships with UF entities, national organizations, and early childhood researchers and practitioners to bridge research, policy, and practice.
Funding and Resource Development: Secure a broad array of external funding (e.g., grants, contracts, gifts) and partnerships to support the Center's initiatives. Expand the Center's impact by identifying and pursuing new opportunities, building capacity, and ensuring the sustainability of its initiatives.
Mentorship and Professional Development: Mentor faculty, graduate students, and postdoctoral associates contributing to programmatic and faculty development.
ABOUT THE COLLEGE: The College of Education at the University of Florida, founded in 1906, has consistently been ranked No. 1 and No. 2 in the nation in Online Graduate Education for the last nine years, No. 2 nationally for undergraduate education and 6th nationally among public and private education schools (U.S. News & World Report). Three of the College's academic programs occupy top-20 spots in the U.S. News rankings: Counselor Education (1st), Special Education (4th), and Elementary Education (14th). Cutting-edge interdisciplinary research and public scholarship—often conducted in partnership with other UF colleges, school districts and communities across the state and nation—are yielding powerful learning systems and models that are helping to transform education in today's changing world, starting with our youngest learners. Faculty researchers last year garnered more than $150.3 million in external awards supporting studies and projects addressing education's most critical issues. With both on campus and online options, the college offers 29 bachelor's and advanced degree programs and concentration areas, within nine academic specialties. To sustain the college's innovative edge, heightened emphasis on emerging technologies, student experience and interdisciplinary research will effectively prepare tomorrow's leaders in all education disciplines. The College's educator preparation programs have been continuously nationally accredited since 1954. Follow us: @UF_COE (X), @uf_coe (Instagram), @university-of-florida-college-of-education (LinkedIn), and @UF.COE (Facebook)
ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY: The University of Florida, founded in 1853, is a public land-grant, sea-grant and space-grant research university and one of the most academically diverse universities in the nation. U.S. News & World Report ranks UF 7th among public universities. National rankings such as 1st by the Wall Street Journal and 4th by Forbes in their respective lists of Public Universities are a result of UF's commitment to provide the highest quality education at the best value. UF is home to 16 colleges and more than 200 research, service and education centers, bureaus and institutes, and boasts more than 6,600 faculty members, 60,000 students and 405,000 living alumni. Faculty scholars last year generated more than $1.26 billion in research awards. UF recently launched a $70 million AI partnership with NVIDIA, taking the first step toward ensuring equitable access to bringing AI to students and faculty from across campus and the state. The Florida Legislature designated UF as a “preeminent'' state university in 2013.
ABOUT THE AREA: UF is situated in Gainesville in North Central Florida, a vibrant college town that blends big-city cultural and athletic offerings with small-town friendliness and charm, along with excellent schools. Gainesville, located about halfway between the Atlantic Ocean and Gulf of Mexico, is often recognized as one of America's best college towns and is easily accessible to three major metropolitan areas (Jacksonville, Orlando and Tampa). The National Arbor Day Foundation has recognized Gainesville as a “Tree City USA” every year since 1982. USA Today ranked Gainesville as the number one place to move in the Sunshine State. Add the allure of Florida's famous sunshine, tropical breezes, and abundant wilderness, springs, rivers and seashores nearby, and it is little wonder that top-caliber faculty and students find our College and University to be the perfect balance of premier academics and a fulfilling lifestyle.

The Department of Advertising at the University of Florida College of Journalism and Communications invites applications for a full-time, nine-month scholar at the rank of Associate or Full Professor in Advertising.

The Department of Advertising seeks to hire an associate or full professor engaged in scholarly research and grant acquisitions in the areas of health communication, science communication, environmental communication, or risk communication. Scholars should emphasize mediated or mass communication aspects of these specialties. The successful candidate has built a national or international reputation, via an established research record with publications in top-tier journals and success in securing extramural funding. They are also expected to mentor junior faculty, contribute to the department's leadership, advance the research agenda, and foster collaborations across the College and University and with other national or international institutions.

We seek candidates that can teach undergraduate advertising courses and graduate-level mass communication courses. Preferably, they will demonstrate competency in teaching one or more courses from the core curriculum for the advertising major, especially courses in advertising strategy and advertising campaigns. The Astronomical Space Technology Research Applications Lab (ASTRAL) includes ISO 6+ cleanroom facilities with ISO 4-5 flow bench; an integration vacuum chamber (<1.0E-6 Torr) for space instrument and component performance testing; electrostatic discharge (ESD) flooring and stations; dedicated, ultra-high purity (UHP) gas fixtures; and silicone-free cleanroom spaces for sensitive space experimentation. Faculty at UF also carry out research using the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument and the Sloan Digital Sky Survey V. UF is home to HiPerGator, one of the most powerful high-performance computers at a US public university (www.rc.ufl.edu/services/hipergator/).

Job Description

AST/ASO
Classification Minimum Requirements:
Candidates for Assistant Professor shall hold the highest degree appropriate to their field or possess equivalent qualifications based on professional experience. A candidate shall be expected to demonstrate successful experience pertinent to the position they are being recommended and have demonstrated qualities relevant to the goals of the academic unit in which they will be employed.
Candidates for Associate Professor shall hold the highest degree appropriate to their field or possess professional qualifications above those equivalent to the highest degree relevant to their field. They are expected to have produced creative work, professional writing, or research and successful teaching or professional experience. A candidate for this rank must have a distinguished record of achievement beyond the assistant professor level.
Job Description:
The College of Education at the University of Florida seeks a 9-month assistant or associate tenure-track faculty with expertise in artificial intelligence (AI) in education. This position will be part of the Educational Technology or Research and Evaluation Methodology academic program and UF's Institute for Advanced Learning Technologies.
The faculty member will join a dynamic community of scholars and engage in collaborative work with colleagues across UF and beyond, including but not limited to: the AI2 Center, the UF Artificial Intelligence and Informatics Research Institute, Computer & Information Science & Engineering, Digital Worlds Institute, UF Libraries, McKnight Brain Institute, Neuroscience, Psychology/Cognitive Sciences, Florida Museum of Natural History, Harn Museum of Art and UF Online.
Potential areas of expertise and scholarship include:
Generative AI in teaching and learning
AI and professional learning
AI and educational assessment
AI literacy for learning and instruction across formal and informal education contexts
AI for inclusive and accessible education
AI ethics and policy
Other innovative areas of inquiry related to AI and other emerging learning technologies
Responsibilities:
Conduct scholarly activities commensurate with expectations of tenure-track faculty at an AAU research-intensive university
Vigorously pursue external funding to enhance research and development
Publish in respected refereed scholarly journals salient to the candidate's line of research
Present research at national and international conferences
Advise, engage, and mentor graduate students in research and teaching activities
Teach courses (face-to-face, blended, and/or online)
Provide service to the program, school, college, university, and the profession
ABOUT THE COLLEGE: Founded in 1906, the College of Education at the University of Florida has a long history of mission-driven excellence, working to advance research, prepare the next generation of educators and solve society's most pressing challenges. The college is No. 2 in the nation among all Graduate Education Schools, according to U.S. News & World Report. In Online Graduate Education, the college has ranked No. 1 or No. 2 for the last 11 years. Among specialty rankings, both the Counseling (No. 2) and Special Education (No. 5) programs have maintained top-five designations for the past four years. In total, the college ranks top 20 in six program areas including Elementary Teacher Education (No. 12), Curriculum and Instruction (No. 17), Educational Administration (No. 19) and Higher Education (No. 19). Novel interdisciplinary research and public scholarship—in collaboration with other UF colleges, school districts, communities and education partners across the nation—are yielding powerful real-world results in teaching and learning. Last year, faculty researchers tallied more than $133.4 million in research expenditures supporting studies and projects addressing education's most challenging issues. To sustain the college's innovative edge and societal benefit, heightened emphasis on AI and emerging technologies, student experience and interdisciplinary research will effectively prepare tomorrow's leaders in all education disciplines. With both on-campus and online options, the college offers a variety of bachelor's and advanced degree programs and concentration areas within nine academic specialties. The college's educator preparation programs have been accredited by CAEP and NCATE since 1954. Follow us: @UF_COE (X), @uf_coe (Instagram), @university-of-florida-college-of-education (LinkedIn), and @UF.COE (Facebook)
ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY: The University of Florida, founded in 1853, is a public land-grant, sea-grant and space-grant research university and one of the most academically diverse universities in the nation. U.S. News & World Report ranks UF No. 7 among public universities. National rankings such as No. 1 for Online Bachelor's by U.S. News and No. 1 by the Wall Street Journal are a result of UF's commitment to provide the highest-quality education at the best value. UF is a Carnegie R1 institution, home to 16 colleges and more than 200 research, service and education centers, bureaus and institutes. The university boasts more than 6,100 faculty members, 63,000 students and 525,000 living alumni. Faculty scholars last year generated more than $1.25 billion in research awards. UF recently expanded its $70 million AI partnership with NVIDIA, adding an additional $24 million investment to make AI accessible to students and faculty across campus and the state. The Florida Legislature designated UF as a "preeminent'' state university in 2013.
ABOUT THE AREA: UF is situated in Gainesville, a vibrant college town in North Central Florida that blends big-city cultural and athletic offerings with small-town friendliness and charm, along with excellent schools. Gainesville, located about halfway between the Atlantic Ocean and Gulf of America, is recognized as one of the nation's best college towns and is easily accessible to three major metropolitan areas (Jacksonville, Orlando and Tampa). The National Arbor Day Foundation has recognized Gainesville as a "Tree City USA" every year since 1982. Livability ranked Gainesville as one of the Best Places to Live in the U.S. Add the allure of Florida's famous sunshine, tropical breezes, and abundant wilderness, springs, rivers and seashores nearby, and it is little wonder that top-caliber faculty and students find our university to be the perfect balance of premier academics and a fulfilling lifestyle.

Job Description:
The Department of Psychiatry at UF College of Medicine in Gainesville, Florida is seeking an Assistant, Associate Full Professor in the Division of Addiction Medicine. This is a full-time (1.0 FTE), Clinical Track (non-tenure accruing) faculty position. Appointment rank (Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor) will be commensurate with experience, academic accomplishments, and national recognition, consistent with University of Florida College of Medicine guidelines.
This role provides essential inpatient and outpatient clinical care within the Florida Recovery Center while supporting the Division of Addiction Medicine's academic mission. The faculty member will contribute to medical student and graduate education through teaching, supervision, and mentorship, with opportunities to engage in quality improvement, clinical scholarship, and collaborative research. Depending on experience and interest, the position may also offer leadership opportunities, including program development, faculty mentorship, and participation in divisional strategic initiatives.
The UF Health Florida Recovery Center is Florida's premiere addiction treatment program. Our multidisciplinary treatments are supported by advanced research from stellar facilities, such as the Evelyn F. and William L. McKnight Brain Institute of the University of Florida, where we are uncovering the mechanisms of addiction and are developing new treatments. Our program combines the established principles of recovery and evidence-based addiction treatments with the knowledge and capabilities of a leading academic medical center. Calling upon the skills of board-certified addiction medicine specialists, as well as psychiatrists and licensed behavioral health counselors, treatment encompasses the physical, emotional and spiritual aspects of recovery followed by the well-established and proven 12-step method.
The successful applicant for this position will report to the Chief of the Division of Addiction Medicine.

The University of Florida School of Music in the College of the Arts invites applications for a full-time, 9-month Assistant Professor in the Bands area with an appointment starting August 16, 2027. We seek an accomplished pedagogue who will contribute to the continued success and growth of a comprehensive band program. The successful candidate will instruct concert and athletic ensembles, bringing a dynamic personality and enthusiasm for teaching to our existing community of outstanding scholars and musicians.
The University of Florida College of the Arts intends to be a transformative community, responding to and generating paradigmatic shifts in the arts and beyond. As artists and scholars, we embrace the complexity of our evolving human experience and seek to empower our students and faculty to shape that experience fearlessly through critical study, creative practice, and provocation. We seek a colleague who identifies as a change-maker. We seek a colleague who will position emerging artists and researchers as catalysts for justice on local and global levels.

Responsibilities:
Tenure Accruing Responsibilities
• Collaborate with the Director of Bands and Associate Director of Bands in the day-to-day operations of the band program, ensuring effective rehearsals, performances, and administrative coordination.
• Assist with the planning, preparation, and execution of performances, including concerts, athletic events, tours, and special programs.
• Conduct and rehearse assigned concert bands, athletic bands, and related ensembles in support of the artistic and educational mission of the band program.
• Teach undergraduate conducting courses.
• Collaborate with band faculty and staff on scheduling, equipment coordination, and ensemble logistics.
• Support recruitment, retention, and outreach activities for the band program and School of Music.
• Participate in service activities appropriate to a tenure-accruing faculty appointment, including faculty meetings and School of Music events.
• Perform additional duties as assigned in support of the mission and goals of the band program and School of Music.
Summer Faculty Appointment Responsibilities
• Beginning on the first day of each Summer B session and continuing through the start of Fall classes, assist with planning and preparations for the band program.
SCHOOL OF MUSIC: Organized within the College of the Arts, the School of Music plays an important role in the academic and cultural life of the University, the College's Creative Campus initiative and the community. The School has 40 full-time and nine adjunct faculty, serving some 200 graduate and 200 undergraduate music majors. Degree programs include B.S., B.A., B.M., M.M., D.M.A., and the Ph.D. in music education, composition, ethnomusicology, and historical musicology. Program emphases include performance, music education, theory, composition, music history and literature, ethnomusicology, conducting, and sacred music. The School of Music is also home to the UF Bands program, which includes “The Pride of the Sunshine” Gator Marching Band. School of Music facilities include the School of Music Building and Steinbrenner Band Hall, among others. The University of Florida is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges and is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music. We foster an environment where novel creative practice, leading research, and experiential learning thrive. Our students, faculty, and staff interrogate and respond to the ever-changing relationship between technology and the human spirit. We prepare future leaders in artistic professions and creative industries, while developing student capacity for interdisciplinary scholarship that serves and engages local and global communities. The College offers baccalaureate, masters, and doctoral degrees. Approximately 1,600 students are pursuing majors in degrees offered by the College of the Arts under the direction of 150 faculty members in its three accredited schools— the School of Art + Art History, the School of Music, and the School of Theatre + Dance, and in the Center for Arts in Medicine, the Digital Worlds Institute, and the Center for Arts, Migration, and Entrepreneurship. Job Description:
The Office of Research Affairs at the University of Florida College of Medicine Jacksonville invites applications for a full-time faculty position at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level to further grow our research focus on implementation science. We are seeking established, extramurally-funded implementation scientist(s) who will expand our engagement of the health issues that affect the population we serve and also provide value-add to our existing federally funded programs in the areas of respiratory health, neurorehabilitation, and/or population genomics. As our mission is to translate groundbreaking research to our patients and community, implementation science is a key area of focus for our college. This is an excellent opportunity to join a vibrant academic community and contribute to advancing research within a supportive, interdisciplinary environment.
This position offers opportunities for both tenured and non-tenured academic tracks, depending on the candidate's experience, background, and whether or not the candidate is a clinician.
The University of Florida College of Medicine - Jacksonville's research ecosystem is thriving with a growing reputation in the southeast and nationally. Over the last five years, total funding has grown by 63% through strategic integration with the main campus in Gainesville, investments on access to healthcare data, enhanced data analytics (through our Center for Data Solutions), and machine learning through partnerships with the University of Florida's Integrated Data Repository and HiPerGator high performance computing system. To support successful candidates, the Office of Research Affairs houses robust services for grant management, finances and compliance as well as patient recruitment/follow-up, industry clinical trials, entrepreneurship, and research training.
The UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville (UF COMJ) is the largest of the three colleges at the Health Science Center Jacksonville. We excel in education, research and patient care that expresses our steadfast values of compassion, excellence, professionalism and innovation. The college's 16 clinical science departments house more than 450 faculty members, 1,560 staff and 384 residents and fellows, as well as medical students from UF and around the country. We offer an incredible breadth of clinical training programs and proud to a recognized leader in human subjects research in northeast Florida and the southeast region. Research, discovery and innovation are critical aspects of our campus and we have some of the country's leading researchers exploring new ways to promote health and wellness for the patients and communities we serve.

Research, discovery and innovation are critical aspects of our clinical campus and we have some of the country's leading researchers at our locations searching for and finding new treatments and clinical options.

With over 1,100 miles of navigable waterways, Jacksonville offers more shoreline than any other city in the nation – ideal for boating, fishing, and water sports.
The city is a hub of vibrant culture and entertainment, hosting the second-largest jazz festival in the U.S., a rich musical history that includes legendary names like Lynyrd Skynyrd, and Ray Charles, and lively arts and food scenes. Job Description:
The Department of History in the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences at the University of Florida invites applications for a full-time (1FTE), nine-month, non-tenure-accruing position in United States history and Assistant Director of the Samuel Proctor Oral History Program (SPOHP), at the rank of Lecturer, with the working title of Assistant Director/Assistant Instructional Professor. The appointment will begin on August 16, 2027.
The successful candidate will play a key leadership role in advancing SPOHP's mission of teaching, training, research, and public engagement. Working closely with faculty, staff, and students, the Assistant Director will help foster student development through experiential learning opportunities and provide leadership in oral history training and project-based scholarship. The candidate will also contribute to the Department of History's vibrant intellectual community and commitment to innovative, student-centered teaching.
Drawing on expertise in oral history, public history, and United States history, the successful candidate will teach a 2-2 course load that includes courses in oral history methodology, public history, and areas of U.S. history that complement SPOHP's mission and support the curricular needs of the Department. Teaching responsibilities should emphasize active, hands-on learning and engage students in oral history research, community partnerships, digital and public humanities initiatives, and other forms of applied historical practice.
As Assistant Director, the successful candidate will oversee SPOHP's internship program, including intern recruitment, training, mentorship, and supervision. The Assistant Director will also develop and lead oral history workshops for students and public audiences; help coordinate public programs, outreach, and communications; and contribute to the development and implementation of grant- and contract-funded projects as opportunities arise. The position will work closely with the SPOHP Director, program staff, faculty, and campus and community partners.
The Samuel Proctor Oral History Program is an award-winning, nationally respected program that has been a cornerstone of the University of Florida campus for six decades. SPOHP advances oral history research, teaching, and public engagement; provides significant experiential-learning opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students; and stewards a collection of more than 10,000 oral histories and sound recordings. The Assistant Director will join a professional staff of five, along with undergraduate and graduate assistants, and will play a significant role in the program's next chapter.
The successful candidate will have the opportunity to benefit from the support, resources, and activities of relevant programs across the University of Florida, including the Center for the Humanities and the Public Sphere, UF Libraries,

Job Description:
The Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences is creating an environment that affirms community across all dimensions. Duties and Responsibilities
This is a 12-month 100% (1.0 FTE) administration position. The Center Director is the administrative head of the North Florida Research and Education Center (NFREC) and provides leadership and support for research, extension and teaching programs essential to the agricultural, natural resource conservation, environmental and consumer interests of the area encompassing the eastern Florida Panhandle through the Suwanee Valley and much of NE Florida. A key component of success in the Director position is stakeholder engagement across these areas that will unify efforts toward common interests and identify stakeholder needs. The Director is responsible for encouraging development of proactive programs addressing present and future needs of surrounding agricultural, natural resource and urban communities. NFREC programs seek to improve the viability of regional agricultural economics, protect and enhance natural resources, support sound urban landscape practices and encourage positive interests at the urban-agricultural interface.
The Center Director is responsible for effective management of NFREC resources - most importantly budgetary and personnel management - and for development of short- and long-term goals involving programs, equipment, physical plant and personnel. The Center Director is to actively seek private funding and endowments to enhance the sustainability of the NFREC. Encouraging and supporting faculty to seek extramural grant opportunities is a key job requirement. The Center Director will liaison with local, state, and federal agencies and will interact with UF/IFAS administration, county extension faculty, other UF faculty and staff, and agricultural and environmental leaders in accordance with the Center's mission and goals. The Center Director is expected to use appropriate communication and management skills to promote teamwork among faculty and staff, delegate responsibilities to associate center directors at the three NFREC locations as appropriate and make timely decisions. The Director is responsible for evaluation of NFREC faculty programs and initiation of tenure and promotion actions in consultation with department chairs and also must actively engage in filling positions after retirement on established programs. The Center Director is expected to work strongly towards establishing new faculty positions and programs with a clear vision for future agriculture and natural resource development goals for the region and the state. The Center Director will form stakeholder advisory committees, composed of clientele, to assist with program related recommendations and decisions and to generate support for needed facilities and equipment. The Center Director should initiate and encourage cooperative research projects with national and international institutions. The Center Director reports directly to the Vice President for Agriculture and Natural Resources and is responsible programmatically to the Deans for Academic Programs, Research and Extension.
The Center Director must take an active role to develop and maintain goodwill for the Center among various support and clientele groups, local agencies, and consumers. Strong ties must be developed and maintained with commodity organizations, regulatory agencies, environmental groups and local and statewide governmental agencies. The Director will cooperate with UF/IFAS Department Chairs, other UF/IFAS Research and Education Center directors, county extension faculty and other UF units in program development.
Background Information
The North Florida Research & Education Center (NFREC) is one of the largest and most diverse off-campus units of UF/IFAS, consisting of campuses in Quincy, Marianna and Live Oak in the eastern Panhandle and Big Bend Region of Florida. The Quincy campus established in 1921 is a 1,021-acre research and education facility located in Gadsden County. The NFREC-Marianna, a 1,288-acre facility, was originally one of the Mobile Units established in 1941 and made its permanent home in Jackson County in 1948. The NFREC-Suwannee Valley (Live Oak) consists of 388 acres, was created by the Florida Legislature in 1947 and began operation on November 1, 1950. The NFREC has 16 faculty members located at Quincy and Marianna that represent nine academic units (agronomy, animal science, entomology, environmental horticulture, forestry, horticulture, plant pathology, soil and water science, and wildlife conservation). Four Regional Specialized Extension Agents (RSA) are located at the NFREC-Suwannee Valley specialized in row crops, rural and agribusiness development, vegetable crops, and water resources, and one RSA is located at Quincy specialized in water resources. Research and Extension programs are collaborative, with a system-based focus on cropping systems, biofuel and medicinal crops, beef/forage production systems, plant breeding systems, specialty crop systems and natural resource management systems. The Center Director's office is located at Quincy with Marianna 40 miles to the west and Live Oak 100 miles to the east. Faculty members commonly use facilities at all three campuses. The NFREC is characterized by a dynamic population of post-doctoral associates, graduate students, scientific, farm, and administrative staff. This variety of faculty, staff and programs provides a unique setting for transdisciplinary research that ties the NFREC with faculty on the main UF campus, faculty at other Research and Education Centers around the state, as well as other universities across the nation. The NFREC also has a strong presence internationally with many faculty members involved in research, extension and teaching in many countries in South America, Europe, Africa and Asia.

This is a 9-month tenure-accruing position that will be 70% research (Florida Agricultural Experiment Station) and 30% extension (Florida Cooperative Extension Service), based at the Agricultural AI Institute within the Gulf Coast Research and Education Center (GCREC), Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences, at the University of Florida. This assignment may change in accordance with the needs of the unit. Tenure will accrue in the Department of Horticultural Sciences. The faculty member is expected to develop an externally funded research and Extension program in their area of expertise.
The position is part of a cohort of new hires for the GCREC Agricultural AI Institute that will focus on the development, advancement, and deployment of applied artificial intelligence (AI) in agriculture with an emphasis on automation and efficiency in specialty crop production.
The successful candidate will advance the Institute's research mission by developing, validating, and deploying artificial intelligence (AI) innovations into field-ready agricultural technologies that address crop production challenges including, but not limited to, weed, disease, and insect detection, nutrient deficiency identification, crop characterization, and yield estimation. The successful candidate will develop, adapt, and integrate AI models into production systems for targeted spraying, precision mapping, spatial analysis, sensor-based automation, and other advanced agricultural uses.
The faculty member will play a key role in technology transfer by collaborating with multidisciplinary faculty, growers, equipment manufacturers, and agricultural technology companies to deploy and evaluate AI-enabled systems. Responsibilities include coordinating field demonstrations, providing technical expertise during implementation, collecting engineering and performance feedback, and supporting the refinement of technologies as they progress toward commercial readiness.
The extension component will include the development of a successful educational program to accelerate commercial adoption and evaluation of AI-based agricultural technologies with the goal of improving the profitability and environmental sustainability of Florida's fruit and vegetable industry. Examples of extension include workshops with growers, field days, online resources, county extension partnerships, extension publications, and decision-support systems.
Candidates with strong academic backgrounds that also demonstrate the ability to work with applied systems will be preferred. The candidate will have the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary environment consisting of industry partners and faculty in agricultural and biological engineering, economics, entomology, horticulture, microbiology, plant pathology, soil science, and weed science. A successful candidate is expected to embrace all three missions the Land-grant university system: Research, Extension, and Teaching.
The candidate is required to establish a strong, externally funded, research program, and promote their research activity and leadership in professional societies as well as sustained publication activity in top scientific journals. The candidate is encouraged to collaborate with other faculty and research partners, creating synergy both inside and outside of the University of Florida.
The successful candidate will participate actively in undergraduate and graduate education by chairing and serving on graduate committees, supervising thesis, dissertation and undergraduate research, and publishing research results with students. Faculty are encouraged to participate in professional development activities related to teaching and advising and may teach courses and seminars.

The University of Florida's Gulf Coast Research and Education Center (GCREC) is a nationally recognized hub for interdisciplinary research, Extension, and graduate education supporting Florida's specialty crop industries. The Center is in Wimauma, approximately 35 minutes from downtown Tampa. GCREC is home to more than 20 faculty whose expertise spans artificial intelligence, automation, engineering, geomatics, horticulture, plant breeding, plant pathology, entomology, horticulture, national resource management, and precision agriculture. The center offers exceptional research infrastructure, including modern laboratories and offices, greenhouses, approximately 500 acres of research farm, and housing for up to 34 graduate students.
This position will be housed in the new Agricultural AI Institute, a state-of-the-art research facility dedicated to advancing artificial intelligence, robotics, automation, and precision agriculture for specialty crop production. The Institute is designed to foster innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration, and features newly constructed offices, collaborative research space, advanced engineering and computer science laboratories, fabrication and prototyping shops, and dedicated training facilities. The Agricultural AI Institute provides an exceptional environment for developing transformative technologies while working alongside leading researchers, students, and industry partners to shape the future of agriculture.
The University of Florida's Horticultural Sciences Department is a nationally recognized leader in teaching, research, and Extension dedicated to advancing the science and practice of specialty crop production. As one of the largest and most comprehensive horticultural programs in the United States, the department conducts interdisciplinary research spanning fruit and vegetable crops, environmental horticulture, plant breeding and genetics, precision agriculture, controlled environment production, artificial intelligence, automation, and sustainable production systems. Faculty collaborate closely with growers, industry partners, and government agencies to develop innovative, science-based solutions that enhance agricultural productivity, profitability, and environmental stewardship while preparing the next generation of leaders in horticultural science.
The University of Florida is a Land-Grant, Sea-Grant, and Space-Grant institution, encompassing virtually all academic and professional disciplines, with an enrollment of more than 56,000 students. UF is a member of The Association of American Universities. The Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences includes the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences, the Florida Agricultural Experiment Station, the Florida Cooperative Extension Service, the College of Veterinary Medicine, the Florida Sea Grant program, and encompasses 16 on-campus academic departments and schools, 12 Research and Educational Centers (REC) located throughout the state, 6 Research sites/demonstration units administered by RECs or academic departments, and Florida Cooperative Extension Service offices in all 67 counties (counties operate and maintain). The School of Natural Resources and Environment is an interdisciplinary unit housed in IFAS and managed by several colleges on campus. UF/IFAS employs nearly 4,500 people, which includes approximately 990 salaried faculty and 1,400 permanent support personnel located in Gainesville and throughout the state. IFAS, one of the nation's largest agricultural and natural resources research and education organizations, is administered by a Vice President and four deans: the Dean of the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences, the Dean for Extension and Director of the Florida Cooperative Extension Service, the Dean for Research and Director of the Florida Agricultural Experiment Station, and the Dean for the College of Veterinary Medicine. UF/IFAS also engages in cooperative work with Florida A&M University in Tallahassee.

Candidates should have demonstrated excellence in verbal and written communication skills, and proven ability to participate in collaborative efforts and procurement of external funding. Experience with machine learning, computer vision, and/or experience with AI deployment in agricultural systems is necessary. Candidates must be supportive of the mission of the University Land-Grant system. Candidates must also have a commitment to UF core values.
Preferred:

The Department of Psychiatry at the University of Florida College of Medicine invites applications for a full-time (1.0 FTE) tenure‑track Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor to serve as Director of the UF Center for Autism and Neurodevelopment (UF CAN). The ideal candidate will bring a strong vision for advancing innovative, integrated services while fostering collaborative relationships across clinical, research, and community stakeholders.
This role offers a unique opportunity to lead a multidisciplinary team in advancing statewide initiatives in clinical services, education, research, and advocacy. The Director will oversee strategic planning, program innovation, and operational excellence, while fostering collaboration across university departments, state agencies, and peer institutions. The position also includes opportunities for direct clinical care, teaching, and research—making it ideal for a candidate passionate about improving outcomes for neurodiverse individuals and their families.

Oversee the daily operations of the University of Florida Center for Autism and Neurodevelopment (UF CAN), ensuring high standards of service delivery and organizational efficiency.
Develop and implement strategic plans to elevate program quality, visibility, and statewide impact.
Promote a culture of excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement across all areas of the Center.

Proven experience and success working with Autism and Neurodivergent individuals.

Represent the Center at national conferences and in partnerships with peer institutions.
Lead the coordinating efforts and collaborate with the statewide Centers for Autism and Related Disorders (CARD) by supporting integration and alignment of information dissemination across the state.

Job Description:
The Herbert Wertheim College of Engineering at the University of Florida invites nominations and applications for the position of Professor and Department Chair of the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (MAE). Reporting to the Dean of the Herbert Wertheim College of Engineering, the Chair will provide strategic, intellectual, and administrative leadership for an internationally visible research and education enterprise. The successful candidate will be an accomplished scholar and an effective organizational leader with a strong record of externally funded research who can substantially improve the department's recognition and ranking, develop a clear vision for international impact and connect the department's strengths to consequential opportunities for Florida and the world. The selected leader will join the Dean's leadership team and will be expected to advance both the department and the college, contribute to university priorities, and engage constructively with the state, nation, and profession.
The Department of Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering (MAE) is the largest degree-granting unit at UF. The Department has nearly 60 faculty members, 500 graduate students and 3,100 undergraduates. In 2025, annual research expenditures reached $28M with 15 active grants over $1 million. Among public universities, Aerospace Engineering is currently ranked No. 16 and Mechanical Engineering is currently ranked No. 21 in the 2026 U.S. News & World Report rankings. Traditional strengths in solid mechanics, design, thermal fluid systems, dynamics and controls are leveraged in interdisciplinary and cutting-edge efforts in autonomous systems, multiphase turbulent systems, novel energy systems, bioengineering, advanced manufacturing, computational science, and space systems. MAE is home to nearly 20 student societies and provides exceptional dedicated facilities and financial support for our student-led design/build/compete organizations that routinely capture top placement at national and international competitions.
In addition to overseeing the operational management of the Department, responsibilities of the Chair include:
Creating a compelling vision for the advancement of the department that fosters cutting edge research within a collaborative and multidisciplinary environment and connects existing strengths to consequential opportunities.
Recruiting faculty and facilitating both the professional and scholarly growth of the faculty, particularly the junior faculty.
Ensuring a premier educational experience that fosters success of all trainees (undergraduate, graduate, postdoctoral and researchers).
Elevating the awareness of the department's impact and enhancing the working partnerships with leaders of UF, government agencies, and industry.
Increasing sponsored research, private and external funding opportunities for the department.
Cultivating corporate, governmental, alumni and other private donations.
Ensuring an exceptional culture of collaboration, respect and continuous improvement for faculty, staff and students.
The Chair will have the opportunity to build upon MAE's substantial research and educational strengths, shape its future strategic directions, and work closely with college leadership to advance ambitious initiatives in faculty excellence, research, and education.

In addition to clinical responsibilities, the individual will also be involved with training pediatric residents and will assume responsibility for restructuring and facilitating the Adolescent Medicine Rotation. The faculty member will be encouraged to participate in quality improvement work and to collaborate with other members of the department on clinical research projects. There is an expectation to participate fairly in on-call rotation for evening and after hours call.
This position will report to the Chief of the Division of General Academic Pediatrics and Chair of the Department of Pediatrics at the University of Florida College of Medicine – Jacksonville.
The University of Florida College of Medicine-Jacksonville is the largest of the three colleges at the Health Science Center Jacksonville. The college is affiliated with UF Health in Jacksonville, a health system comprised of two hospitals — the 603-bed UF Health Jacksonville and 92-bed UF Health North — and more than 60 primary and specialty care practices throughout Northeast Florida and Southeast Georgia.
The college's 16 clinical science departments house more than 440 faculty members, 1,560 staff and 384 residents and fellows, as well as medical students from UF and around the country. We offer an incredible breadth of clinical training program sand proud to train many of best primary care providers and specialists throughout the region, the state and the country.
The college offers 38 accredited graduate medical education programs and 14 non-standard programs. More than 100 residents and fellows from programs across the U.S. come to UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville to participate in various clinical rotations as well.
In addition to graduate medical education, clinical rotations in all the major disciplines are provided for students from the UF College of Medicine in Gainesville. Third-year medical students enrolled at UF spend about 25 percent of their training at the Jacksonville campus, gaining valuable experience in an urban setting. While third-year rotations are only offered to UF students, elective rotations in the final year of clinical training are available to students from accredited schools in the US and Canada.
For practicing physicians, the college offers a continuing medical education program that recruits national and international speakers who are well known and respected in their fields.
The college's faculty, residents and fellows are active in clinical research. Residents and fellows regularly present their findings at locations across the country and publish their projects in well-known publications. In 2019, the campus received $23.1 million in external research funding, approximately 50% of which was federally sponsored projects.
The campus houses a 16,000-square-foot clinical and translational research facility. To support faculty and resident research, the college has a Center for Data Solutions, offering researchers analytics, epidemiology and biostatistics support, and a Center for Research Training, helping develop the next generation of highly collaborative clinical researchers.
Located in the Northeastern part of the state on the Atlantic Ocean, Jacksonville's weather is sunny and pleasant. We enjoy an average of 320 days of sunshine each year, yet have the coolest summers in the state. Known as the River City, Jacksonville is a major port city with numerous waterways, two Naval bases, several nature preserves, marshes, lakes, wetlands and miles of beaches. Flowing through Jacksonville is the 310-mile St. Johns River, which plays a major role in our work and play.
To learn more about our college, our leadership and our campus, please visit us at https://med.jax.ufl.edu/about/.

Classification Title:
SCHOOL DIRECTOR & PROFESSOR
Classification Minimum Requirements:
• An earned doctorate in civil, coastal, environmental, oceanographic engineering, or a closely related field.
• A distinguished record of scholarship, education, mentoring, and professional contribution that merits appointment as a tenured full professor at the University of Florida.
• Evidence of successful leadership in a research-intensive university or comparably complex organization, including building collaborative, high-performing organizational cultures and developing faculty, staff, and emerging leaders.
• Demonstrated ability to develop and articulate a compelling strategic vision to advance the reputation and ranking of the department by translating that vision into clear priorities, strategic investments and measurable outcomes.
• Is skilled in the development and expansion of sponsored research programs, including fostering collaborative research and advancing high-impact programs.
• Excellent communication, judgment, integrity, and relationship-building skills; ability to communicate and work effectively with faculty, staff, students, administrators, and external stakeholders.
• Demonstrated commitment to student success and to a scholarly and working environment where people with varied backgrounds and perspectives can contribute and thrive.
• Experience with external engagement and development, such as industry partnerships, alumni outreach, and fundraising.
Job Description:
The Herbert Wertheim College of Engineering at the University of Florida invites nominations and applications for the position of Professor and Director of the Engineering School of Sustainable Infrastructure and Environment (ESSIE). Reporting to the Dean of the Herbert Wertheim College of Engineering, the Director will provide strategic, intellectual, and administrative leadership for an internationally visible research and education enterprise. The successful candidate will be an accomplished scholar and an effective organizational leader with a strong record of externally funded research who can substantially improve the department's recognition and ranking, develop a clear vision for international impact and connect the department's strengths to consequential opportunities for Florida and the world. The selected leader will join the Dean's leadership team and will be expected to advance both the School and the college, contribute to university priorities, and engage constructively with the state, nation, and profession.
The Director will have the opportunity to shape the future of a multidisciplinary School that integrates expertise across civil, coastal, environmental, sustainability and resilience related engineering and science disciplines; strengthen a culture of collaboration and excellence; elevate the School's national and international visibility; and position ESSIE to address some of the most consequential civil, coastal, and environmental challenges facing Florida, the nation, and the world.
The Opportunity
ESSIE brings together the Department of Civil & Coastal Engineering (https://essie.ufl.edu/cce/) and the Department of Environmental Engineering Sciences (https://essie.ufl.edu/ees/), creating a distinctive academic community that connects built and natural environments.
The School includes approximately 65 faculty and 966 students, with approximately $19 million in annual research expenditures and $22.6 million in research awards. Its research and educational activities extend well beyond traditional disciplines to pioneer research, education, and environmentally responsible engineering technologies that advance innovative solutions that enhance the resilience and sustainability of communities, infrastructure and environmental resources. Through a nexus of the civil, coastal, environmental and oceanographic programs, ESSIE fosters interdisciplinary collaboration across engineering, science, policy and practice.
The School houses and manages a robust network of researchers, research centers, and core facilities (https://essie.ufl.edu/about/research-centers-facilities/), providing exceptional opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration, external partnerships, technology development and high-impact research. These assets represent a major institutional strength and will be central to advancing the School strategic vision and impact under its next Director.
The Director will join ESSIE at a moment of significant opportunity. Urgent challenges and emerging opportunities in infrastructure systems, climate resilience, environmental systems, environmental health engineering, artificial intelligence and automation, advanced materials, mobility, and data-driven engineering are creating new possibilities for research, education, and societal impact. At the same time, UF's breadth, scale, land-grant mission, statewide presence, and interdisciplinary research ecosystem provide an exceptional platform for building ambitious programs and partnerships.
The Director will be expected to articulate a compelling vision for its future and translate that vision into measurable outcomes that strengthens ESSIE's reputation and impact, at the state, national and global levels.
Leadership Priorities
The Director will work with faculty, staff, students, College leadership, alumni, and external partners to advance a focused set of strategic priorities. In collaboration with center directors, facility managers and faculty, the Director will help leverage ESSIE's extensive network of research centers and facilities to attract and strengthen external funding, partnerships, and workforce development opportunities.
● Provide visionary and strategic leadership. Develop and communicate a bold, forward-looking vision for ESSIE that builds on its existing strengths while identifying emerging areas in which the School can achieve distinctive national and international leadership. Translate that vision into clear priorities, measurable goals, strategic investments, and sustained execution.
● Forge a transdisciplinary, cutting-edge research environment by facilitating active collaboration among researchers and units. Provide strategic guidance in identifying and pursuing emerging research opportunities across disciplines. School-wide priorities and the long-term success of ESSIE should guide decisions regarding investments, opportunities, and resources. The Director will encourage ambitious interdisciplinary research, enable faculty to pursue large and complex sponsored programs, strengthen connections among ESSIE's departments, centers and facilities, expand collaborations with UF institutes and centers, and develop strategic partnerships with federal and state agencies, industry, communities, and other universities.
● Recruit, develop, and retain talent. Lead efforts to recruit, develop, and retain outstanding faculty and staff and foster an environment in which people at all career stages can thrive. The Director will promote effective mentoring, professional development, recognition, succession planning, and leadership development while maintaining high expectations for excellence. The Director will also work with College leadership to identify opportunities for strategic faculty growth in areas that strengthen the School's long-term research and educational mission.
● Advance educational innovation and student success. Provide leadership for undergraduate, graduate, and professional education across ESSIE. The Director will support continuous improvement and accreditation; encourage curricular innovation; expand experiential, field-based, interdisciplinary, and research-centered learning opportunities; strengthen graduate education and mentoring; and prepare students to lead in a rapidly changing engineering profession.
● Expand external engagement and advancement. Serve as a visible and persuasive ambassador for ESSIE. The Director will cultivate strong relationships with alumni, industry, government agencies, professional organizations, communities, donors, and other external partners. The Director will work closely with College leadership and advancement professionals to expand philanthropic support and develop partnerships that advance the School's strategic goals.
Expected Salary:
Commensurate with Education and Experience
Required Qualifications:
• An earned doctorate in civil, coastal, environmental, oceanographic engineering, or a closely related field.
• A distinguished record of scholarship, education, mentoring, and professional contribution that merits appointment as a tenured full professor at the University of Florida.
• Evidence of successful leadership in a research-intensive university or comparably complex organization, including building collaborative, high-performing organizational cultures and developing faculty, staff, and emerging leaders.
• Demonstrated ability to develop and articulate a compelling strategic vision to advance the reputation and ranking of the department by translating that vision into clear priorities, strategic investments and measurable outcomes.
• Is skilled in the development and expansion of sponsored research programs, including fostering collaborative research and advancing high-impact programs.
• Excellent communication, judgment, integrity, and relationship-building skills; ability to communicate and work effectively with faculty, staff, students, administrators, and external stakeholders.
• Demonstrated commitment to student success and to a scholarly and working environment where people with varied backgrounds and perspectives can contribute and thrive.
• Experience with external engagement and development, such as industry partnerships, alumni outreach, and fundraising.
Preferred:
• Experience recruiting, mentoring, evaluating, and retaining faculty and staff across career stages and appointment types.
• Experience developing multidisciplinary initiatives, major collaborative proposals, centers, institutes, or other large-scale research activities.
• Experience building productive industry partnerships, including sponsored research, consortia, or public-private collaborations.
• Experience using industry engagement to strengthen education, experiential learning, workforce preparation, and research opportunities.
• The ability to identify emerging funding opportunities and organize faculty and external partners around them.
• Experience working with College and University leadership and across academic units.
• Experience in advancement, philanthropy, alumni engagement, or development of external resources.
• Professional leadership and service in civil, coastal, environmental, oceanographic engineering, or a closely related field or a related discipline.

Applications must be submitted through UFCareers at: https://explore.jobs.ufl.edu/en-us/listing/ (Search Job 541813). Complete applications must include the following files in PDF format: (1) A cover letter describing the candidate's interest in the position, relevant academic leadership experience, and scholarly background; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) the names, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses of five professional references; (Additional required documents should be uploaded as one PDF to the “other documents” section in the application.); (4) a leadership vision statement of no more than 3 pages detailing your leadership approach, a preliminary vision for the department, and two or three strategic priorities the candidate would explore with the community. Competitive candidates are expected to clearly complement the overall mission of the department and the college. The anticipated start date for this position is August 16, 2027. We foster an environment where novel creative practice, leading research, and experiential learning thrive. Our students, faculty, and staff interrogate and respond to the ever-changing relationship between technology and the human spirit. CHAIR & PROFESSOR, Chemical Engineering
Job No: 541748
Work Type: Full Time

Job Description
Classification Title:
Chair & Professor
Classification Minimum Requirements:
An earned doctorate in chemical engineering or a closely related field.
A distinguished record of scholarly research, education, mentoring, and professional contribution that merits appointment as a tenured full professor at the University of Florida.
Evidence of successful leadership in a research-intensive university or comparably complex organization, including building collaborative, high-performing organizational cultures and developing faculty, staff, and emerging leaders.
Demonstrated ability to develop and articulate a compelling strategic vision to advance the reputation and ranking of the department by translating that vision into clear priorities, strategic investments and measurable outcomes.
Is skilled in the development and expansion of sponsored research programs, including fostering collaborative research and advancing high-impact programs.
Excellent communication, judgment, integrity, and relationship-building skills; ability to communicate and work effectively with faculty, staff, students, administrators, and external stakeholders.
Demonstrated commitment to student success and to a scholarly and working environment where people with varied backgrounds and perspectives can contribute and thrive.
Experience with external engagement and development, such as industry partnerships, alumni outreach, and fundraising.
Job Description:
The next Chair will join the Department at an important point in its development. The Department has 25 tenured and tenure-track faculty members, 6 instructional faculty members, and 17 affiliate faculty members. It enrolls more than 70 Ph.D. students, approximately 15 M.S. students, and over 475 undergraduate students in an ABET accredited program. Faculty conduct experimental and computational research in materials science and engineering, biotechnology, and energy systems, with computational as well as experimental focus and with annual research expenditures of approximately $6.5 million.
The Department's primary building is undergoing a comprehensive renovation scheduled for completion in Summer 2027, with more than $44 million in support from the State of Florida. The renovated building will include research laboratories, teaching laboratories, shared facilities, and collaboration spaces. The next Chair will be able to establish an active research program in the renovated building while helping align the new space, faculty strengths, University investments, and external partnerships with the Department's next phase of growth.
The successful candidate will develop a shared vision for the Department and provide the leadership needed to translate that vision into action. This includes identifying areas in which UF Chemical Engineering can lead; developing faculty and future leaders; strengthening research and educational programs; expanding engagement with industry and other external partners; managing human, financial, and physical resources; and positioning the Department to pursue major opportunities beyond the work of any individual faculty member.
Leadership and Department Development
The Chair will work effectively with faculty who bring broad expertise and experience, identify opportunities, establish priorities, build support for those priorities, and create the conditions for faculty, staff, and students to succeed. Key responsibilities include:
Developing and implementing a strategic vision that builds on existing strengths and identifies areas in which UF Chemical Engineering can grow and lead during the next five to ten years.
Translating that vision into priorities for faculty recruitment, research development, educational programs, facilities, partnerships, advancement, and resource allocation.
Recruiting, mentoring, retaining, and supporting outstanding faculty and staff while developing leadership capacity across career stages.
Fostering shared governance, effective communication, collaboration, and accountability while advocating for the Department within HWCOE and across UF.
Research Leadership and External Engagement
The Chair will help increase the scale, impact, and visibility of the Department's research. The successful candidate will bring an established record of competitive federal funding and an understanding of how to develop and sustain strong individual and collaborative programs. Key responsibilities include:
Maintaining an active, externally funded research program while serving as Chair.
Supporting competitive faculty research programs and creating opportunities for multidisciplinary collaboration.
Recognizing emerging opportunities, connecting complementary expertise, and building teams able to compete for major collaborative programs, centers, and institutes.
Facilitating participation in interdisciplinary UF initiatives, including the UF Health Cancer Center, UF Astraeus Space Institute, Florida Semiconductor Institute, and other University research programs.
Strengthening connections with University research infrastructure, other academic units, national and international laboratories, government agencies, foundations, and external partners.
Industry Partnerships and Engagement
The Chair will expand industry engagement as an important component of research growth and student education, strengthening relationships with industries important to Florida and the Southeast while also developing national and international partnerships. Key responsibilities include:
Growing industry-sponsored research and sustained university-industry partnerships that create meaningful opportunities for faculty and students.
Supporting consortia, federal programs, public-private partnerships, and other models that connect academic and industrial expertise.
Expanding industry participation in internships and co-ops, sponsored projects, research experiences, seminars, mentoring, and professional development.
Working with faculty, College leadership, alumni, and industry partners to keep degree programs responsive to evolving technical and workforce needs.
Developing national and international industry relationships that broaden research, education, student placement, and professional opportunities.
Faculty Student and Community Engagement
The Chair will recognize and develop the varied contributions of faculty and staff, create opportunities for individuals to advance shared goals, and cultivate the Department's next generation of academic leaders. Key responsibilities include:
Supporting the professional growth and success of faculty, staff, graduate students, and undergraduate students.
Identifying leadership potential and creating opportunities for rising faculty to contribute to Department, College, University, and professional leadership.
Promoting excellence and innovation in undergraduate and graduate education, mentoring, recruitment, and professional development.
Supporting undergraduate research and meaningful engagement between students and faculty.
Recognizing contributions in research, teaching, mentoring, outreach to Florida schools and communities, professional service, and leadership.
Expected Salary:
Salary is commensurate with education and experience
Required Qualifications:
An earned doctorate in chemical engineering or a closely related field.
A distinguished record of scholarly research, education, mentoring, and professional contribution that merits appointment as a tenured full professor at the University of Florida.
Evidence of successful leadership in a research-intensive university or comparably complex organization, including building collaborative, high-performing organizational cultures and developing faculty, staff, and emerging leaders.
Demonstrated ability to develop and articulate a compelling strategic vision to advance the reputation and ranking of the department by translating that vision into clear priorities, strategic investments and measurable outcomes.
Is skilled in the development and expansion of sponsored research programs, including fostering collaborative research and advancing high-impact programs.
Excellent communication, judgment, integrity, and relationship-building skills; ability to communicate and work effectively with faculty, staff, students, administrators, and external stakeholders.
Demonstrated commitment to student success and to a scholarly and working environment where people with varied backgrounds and perspectives can contribute and thrive.
Experience with external engagement and development, such as industry partnerships, alumni outreach, and fundraising.
Preferred:
Experience recruiting, mentoring, evaluating, and retaining faculty and staff across career stages and appointment types.
Experience developing multidisciplinary initiatives, major collaborative proposals, centers, institutes, or other large-scale research activities.
Experience building productive industry partnerships, including sponsored research, consortia, or public-private collaborations.
Experience using industry engagement to strengthen education, experiential learning, workforce preparation, and research opportunities.
The ability to identify emerging funding opportunities and organize faculty and external partners around them.
Experience working with College and University leadership and across academic units.
Experience in advancement, philanthropy, alumni engagement, or development of external resources.
Professional leadership and service in chemical engineering or a related discipline.
