Complete applications must include the following files in PDF format: (1) A cover letter describing the candidate's interest in the position, relevant academic leadership experience, and scholarly background; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) the names, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses of five professional references. (Additional required documents should be uploaded as one PDF to the “other documents” section in the application.); (4) a leadership vision statement of no more than 3 pages detailing your leadership approach, a preliminary vision for the department, and two or three strategic priorities the candidate would explore with the community. Competitive candidates are expected to clearly complement the overall mission of the department and the college. The anticipated start date for this position is August 16, 2027. Priority consideration will be given to applications received by December 1, 2026. Please direct questions about the position to Senior Associate Dean John M. Shea, Faculty Search Chair, email: jmshea@ufl.edu
About the University of Florida and the Herbert Wertheim College of Engineering
The University of Florida is the flagship institution of the State University System of Florida, a member of the Association of American Universities, and consistently ranked among the nation's leading public universities. UF is currently ranked as one of the top 10 best public universities, 8th according to the 2026 U.S. News & World Report of Best Colleges and is recognized by Forbes as one of 10 public “New Ivies” for producing exceptional graduates. With 16 colleges, more than 150 research centers and institutes, and over 60,000 undergraduate and graduate students, UF is one of the largest universities in the nation. UF offers broad opportunities for interdisciplinary work across engineering, medicine, agriculture, the sciences, and other fields. In FY2026, University of Florida research spending reached a record $1.34 billion. UF is also home to HiPerGator, the fastest AI supercomputer in higher education. The Herbert Wertheim College of Engineering has over 400 faculty members and combines disciplinary depth with cross-cutting institutes, centers, shared facilities, industry partnerships, and a statewide mission.
About the Department
The Department of Chemical Engineering offers ABET accredited B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. degrees in Chemical Engineering. The Department includes 25 primary faculty members, including 6 instructional faculty members, and 17 affiliate faculty members. Current graduate enrollment includes more than 70 Ph.D. students and approximately 15 M.S. students, with over 475 students enrolled in the undergraduate program.
Faculty research spans 7 research thrusts that cover major areas in materials, biotechnology, and energy systems using both computational and experimental methods. UF Chemical Engineering primary faculty include 3 active NIH MIRA Awardees and 3 active NSF CAREER Awardees. Current research is supported by federal agencies including NSF, NIH, DOE, NASA and DARPA, as well as industry, foundations, and other sponsors. These current efforts result in average annual research expenditures are approximately $6.5M.
The Department has substantial opportunities for interdisciplinary research and education across the University of Florida. Growing areas of University investment relevant to Chemical Engineering include biomedical and health-related research through both UF and UF Health initiatives, such as the UF Cancer Center, agricultural efforts though UF IFAS and Extension Offices, space research and technology through the UF Astraeus Space Institute, and semiconductor research, manufacturing, and workforce development through the Florida Semiconductor Institute. Faculty also collaborate broadly across HWCOE and with researchers throughout UF.
For more information about college or department initiatives, visit eng.ufl.edu or che.ufl.edu.

Candidates for Associate Professor shall hold the highest degree appropriate to their field or possess professional qualifications above those equivalent to the highest degree relevant to their field. They are expected to have produced creative work, professional writing, or research and successful teaching or professional experience. A candidate for this rank must have a distinguished record of achievement beyond the assistant professor level.
Job Description:
The University of Florida has pioneered the effort to integrate AI education in every major and every college. The College of Education seeks a tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor in AI-based Quantitative Research Methods in Education. This faculty member will join the Research and Evaluation Methodology program (REM; https://education.ufl.edu/research-evaluation-methods), a productive and collegial community of scholars committed to high-quality teaching, research, and service. In addition, this faculty member will have the opportunity to collaborate with researchers in a variety of units centered around AI and technology-enhanced learning, such as the Institute for Advanced Learning Technologies (https://ialt.education.ufl.edu).
Successful applicants for the tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor position are expected to develop and maintain a clear, systematic line of methodology-focused research; vigorously pursue external research funding; publish in top-tier methodological journals or proceedings; present research findings at meetings of professional associations; and contribute to advising and teaching graduate students. Additionally, candidates will engage in service to the program, school, college, university, and profession in general. The nine-month, tenure-accruing faculty appointment begins August 2027. Salary is negotiable, highly competitive, and commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Potential areas of expertise and scholarship may include:
AI-enhanced psychometrics, Computational Psychometrics, Digital-based assessment, and related areas
Causal machine learning for designing and analyzing experimental and quasi-experimental studies
Reinforcement Learning (RL) in educational research
Natural Language Processing (NLP)-based methods in educational assessment, measurement, and quantitative analysis
Issues of validity, reliability, and heterogeneous impacts in AI-enhanced quantitative methodology
Integration of machine learning and Bayesian or frequentist statistical approaches
Advancements to educational quantitative research methodology through AI
Responsibilities:
Conduct scholarly activities commensurate with expectations of a tenure-track assistant or associate faculty member at a research-intensive university
Build a collaborative and diverse community of scholars among colleagues within and outside of the college, especially within UF's AI research community
Vigorously pursue external funding opportunities with the support of the College's Office of Educational Research
Publish in top-tier refereed methodological journals or proceedings
Advise, engage, and mentor graduate students on research activities and theses and dissertations.
Design and teach advanced methodological courses (face-to-face, blended, and/or online) for graduate students and, potentially, undergraduate students
Provide service to the university and the profession
ABOUT THE COLLEGE: The College of Education at the University of Florida, founded in 1906, has consistently been ranked No. 1 and No. 2 in the nation in Online Graduate Education for the last nine years, No. 2 nationally for undergraduate education and 6th nationally among public and private education schools (U.S. News & World Report). Three of the College's academic programs occupy top-20 spots in the U.S. News rankings: Counselor Education (1st), Special Education (4th), and Elementary Education (14th). Cutting-edge interdisciplinary research and public scholarship—often conducted in partnership with other UF colleges, school districts and communities across the state and nation—are yielding powerful learning systems and models that are helping to transform education in today's changing world, starting with our youngest learners. Faculty researchers last year garnered more than $150.3 million in external awards supporting studies and projects addressing education's most critical issues. With both on campus and online options, the college offers 29 bachelor's and advanced degree programs and concentration areas, within nine academic specialties. To sustain the college's innovative edge, heightened emphasis on emerging technologies, student experience and interdisciplinary research will effectively prepare tomorrow's leaders in all education disciplines. The College's educator preparation programs have been continuously nationally accredited since 1954. ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY: The University of Florida, founded in 1853, is a public land-grant, sea-grant and space-grant research university and one of the most academically diverse universities in the nation. U.S. News & World Report ranks UF 7th among public universities. National rankings such as 1st by the Wall Street Journal and 4th by Forbes in their respective lists of Public Universities are a result of UF's commitment to provide the highest quality education at the best value. UF is home to 16 colleges and more than 200 research, service and education centers, bureaus and institutes, and boasts more than 6,600 faculty members, 60,000 students and 405,000 living alumni. Faculty scholars last year generated more than $1.26 billion in research awards. UF recently launched a $70 million AI partnership with NVIDIA, taking the first step toward ensuring equitable access to bringing AI to students and faculty from across campus and the state. The Florida Legislature designated UF as a “preeminent'' state university in 2013.
ABOUT THE AREA: UF is situated in Gainesville in North Central Florida, a vibrant college town that blends big-city cultural and athletic offerings with small-town friendliness and charm, along with excellent schools. Gainesville, located about halfway between the Atlantic Ocean and Gulf of Mexico, is often recognized as one of America's best college towns and is easily accessible to three major metropolitan areas (Jacksonville, Orlando and Tampa). The National Arbor Day Foundation has recognized Gainesville as a “Tree City USA” every year since 1982. USA Today ranked Gainesville as the number one place to move in the Sunshine State. Add the allure of Florida's famous sunshine, tropical breezes, and abundant wilderness, springs, rivers and seashores nearby, and it is little wonder that top-caliber faculty and students find our College and University to be the perfect balance of premier academics and a fulfilling lifestyle.

Job Title: Part-time and Limited Term Faculty Positions in School of Communication and Media
Location: Kennesaw, Georgia
Regular/Temporary: Regular
Full/Part Time: Part-Time
Job ID: 305226
About Us
For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known for its entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community. A leader in innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State is located just north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of Georgia's largest universities, Kennesaw State offers undergraduate and graduate degrees to over 50,000 students. Our high-impact research and Division I athletics also draw students from throughout the region and across the globe. A member of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State is a Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2) committed to becoming a world-class academic institution positioned to broaden its academic and research missions and expand its scope on a local, regional, and national level.
Our university's vibrant culture, career opportunities, rich benefits, and values of respect, integrity, collaboration, inclusivity, and accountability make us an employer of choice. As part of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State exemplifies the power and promise of a student-centered, research-driven university. In addition, Kennesaw State supports the University of Georgia's core values of accountability, excellence, integrity, and respect. We are searching for talented people to join Kennesaw State University in our vision. For more information, visit the Kennesaw State University website.
Location
Our Kennesaw campus is located at 1000 Chastain Road NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144. Our Marietta campus is located at 1100 South Marietta Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060.
Department Information
The School of Communication & Media prepares ethical, mindful, and effective communicators who combine human skills and technical expertise to pursue fulfilling careers, lead in their communities, tell impactful stories, and grow strong relationships. We blend industry-relevant programs with forward-thinking scholarship to build understanding of the power of communication to innovate, connect, and create.
With more than 400 full-time faculty and 8,100 degree-seeking students, the Norman J. Radow College of Humanities & Social Sciences is dedicated to pioneering workforce readiness in the humanities and social sciences. By staying true to our Liberal Arts values and integrating practical knowledge and experiential learning into our curriculum, we empower our students to become responsible citizens ready for the demands of the modern workplace. The home of three schools and eight departments, the College offers more than 80 graduate and undergraduate programs of study in both traditional and interdisciplinary fields. These programs enable students to develop leadership, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, as well as a strong sense of civic engagement.
The College is committed to the success of our students, faculty, staff and communities. We seek candidates whose experience has prepared them to fulfill that commitment and engage our students, partners, and stakeholders effectively.
Job Summary
Kennesaw State University is now accepting applications for a pool of open rank, part-time and limited term faculty positions in the School of Communication and Media for the academic year 2026-2027. These positions are on an as needed, semester-by-semester basis. Rank is determined at the time of hiring and will be commensurate with credentials. These positions are for work to be performed in the state of Georgia.
Please be advised that Kennesaw State University does not provide any type of visa sponsorship, including transfers, for limited term or part-time faculty.
Responsibilities
Teaching undergraduate courses to support our lower-division and upper-division courses in the broad fields of Journalism & Emerging Media, Media & Entertainment, Organizational & Professional Communication, and Public Relations
Common courses for part-time faculty include Human Communication; Public Speaking; Writing for Public Communication; Communication Law, Ethics, and Diversity; and Digital Media Production
Part-time faculty may be asked to teach in various modalities (face-to-face, hybrid, and online) and courses may be assigned at the Kennesaw or Marietta campus.
Teaching assignments will be based on earned degrees and SACSCOC Faculty Credentials Guidelines.
Required Qualifications
A minimum of a Master's degree, or the foreign equivalent, in Communication, Journalism, Mass Communication, or a closely related discipline is required at the time of hire.
OR
A minimum of a Master's degree, or the foreign equivalent, in a non-related discipline with 18 graduate credit hours in the teaching discipline is required at the time of hire.
Preferred Qualifications
Previous college-level teaching experience
Relevant professional experience
Experience teaching on-line or hybrid courses
Required Documents to Attach
CV
Cover Letter
Unofficial Transcripts (Official Transcripts and Official International Course-by-Course Evaluations Due Upon Hire)
Names, phone numbers, and email addresses of at least 3 references
Evidence of excellence in teaching and/or mentoring, if available. (Candidates who have not taught in a university setting should submit a statement describing how they would leverage their industry experience as part of their teaching philosophy.) (Upload as additional documents).
Incomplete applications will not be considered
Contact Information
For questions about this faculty opening, please contact Chris McCollough, cmccol20@kennesaw.edu.
For technical support or assistance completing a job application, please contact the Shared Services Center at (877) 251-2644 or support@usg.edu.
For questions about a specific job posting at Kennesaw State University, please contact the search chair listed under the contact information section on each posting. For general questions about faculty jobs please email facultyjobs@kennesaw.edu.
USG Core Values
The University System of Georgia is comprised of our 26 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and can be found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18_personnel_conduct.
Additionally, USG supports Freedom of Expression as stated in Board Policy 6.5 Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section6/C2653.

Kennesaw State University is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. The University is committed to maintaining a fair and respectful environment for living, work and study. To that end, and in accordance with federal and state law, Board of Regents policy, and University policy, the University prohibits harassment of or discrimination against any person because of race, color, sex (including sexual harassment, pregnancy, and medical conditions related to pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, ethnicity or national origin, religion, age, genetic information, disability, or veteran or military status by any member of the KSU Community on campus, in connection with a University program or activity, or in a manner that creates a hostile environment for members of the KSU community.
For additional information on this policy, or to file a complaint under the provisions of this policy, students, employees, applicants for employment or admission or other third parties should contact the Office of Institutional Equity at English Building, Suite 225, eeo@kennesaw.edu.

Per the University System of Georgia background check policy, all final candidates will be required to consent to a criminal background investigation. Research experience in applied or computational mathematics and a record of scholarly products produced from such research.

jobs.title: Faculty Positions in Strategic Management and Organisations - Practice (Associate Prof. and Above)
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Overview
School: International Business School Suzhou (IBSS)
Department: Department of Strategic Management and Organisations (SMO)
Position: Associate Professor of Practice / Senior Associate Professor of Practice / Professor of Practice
Location: Suzhou, China
Contract Type: Fixed-term, three-year renewable contract; the third contract is open-ended
Application Review: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the positions are filled. Early applications are therefore strongly encouraged.
ABOUT XJTLU
In 2006, Xi an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU) was founded through a partnership between the University of Liverpool, UK, and Xi an Jiaotong University, China. Offering a unique international education experience, XJTLU brings together excellent research practice and expertise from both institutions and equips students with the skills and knowledge they need to pursue successful careers in a global marketplace. XJTLU now has over 25,000 students studying in Suzhou and Liverpool, approximately 2,500 staff, including more than 1,300 academic staff from over 60 countries, and offers over 120 undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
With a focus on innovative education and research, XJTLU draws on the strengths of its parent universities and plays a pivotal role in facilitating access to China for UK and other international partners. At the same time, XJTLU is exploring future education by blending educational theory, best practice and culture from the West and the East.
This year marks the 20th anniversary of XJTLU. As part of its strategic priorities for the coming decade, the University is entering a new and exciting phase of development. XJTLU continues to innovate in education models and is transitioning from a collection of distinct approaches towards a unified, integrated Academy model a syntegrative ecosystem designed to break down silos, enhance agility and strengthen XJTLU s position at the forefront of global education and research.
For further information about the University, please visit www.xjtlu.edu.cn.
LOCATION
XJTLU is located in the Higher Education Town of Suzhou Industrial Park (SIP), approximately two hours from Shanghai. Suzhou is well connected through nearby international airports and China s high-speed rail network. As a major centre of education, innovation and economic activity, Suzhou combines a rich cultural heritage, including its historic canals and UNESCO World Heritage gardens, with a modern international living environment, excellent amenities and access to international schools.
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS SCHOOL SUZHOU
International Business School Suzhou (IBSS) is growing in size and influence in pursuit of its vision to be a leading international business school. The School is based on the principles of internationalism, innovation, inspiration and integrity, which together ensure a positive impact on society through teaching, research and business engagement. IBSS became the youngest triple crown business school, accredited by AACSB in 2016, EQUIS in 2018 and AMBA/BGA in 2020.
IBSS comprises five departments: Accounting, Economics, Finance, Intelligent Operations and Marketing, and Strategic Management and Organisations. The School has over 180 faculty members and more than 6,000 students from over 60 countries. It delivers undergraduate, postgraduate, IMBA, PhD and Executive Education programmes across all major business disciplines.
ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT
The Department of Strategic Management and Organisations encompasses Strategy, International Business, Human Resource Management, Organisational Behaviour and Leadership. The Department is committed to excellence in student learning, academic research and social impact, and to connecting theory with practice through case-based teaching, applied projects and engagement with business and professional communities.
The Department contributes to undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in Business Administration, International Business with a Language, and Human Resource Management and People Analytics programmes as well as postgraduate students enrolled in the MSc Management or the IMBA programmes. It offers a collegial, internationally oriented environment in which experienced practitioners can translate professional expertise into distinctive learning experiences, applied research and external partnerships.
RESPONSIBILITIES
International Business School Suzhou is not only a research-led business school but also commits itself to empower inclusive and sustainable business via all its activities. In this context, the workload of faculty on Practice Track are generally shared between teaching, practice and service of the School. The Practice Track is intended for faculty whose primary contribution lies in the application, translation, and mobilisation of professional and industry-based expertise in support of the School s teaching, external engagement, student development, and strategic positioning. Practice contribution may take different forms depending on the candidate s expertise, professional network, role, disciplinary area, and the strategic needs of the School. Broadly speaking, Practice Track faculty is expected to contribute to school from the following three broad domains:
a) Business Value - This refers to contribution to business engagement, income generation, partnership development, executive education, consulting, horizontal projects, development projects, professional networks, or other externally oriented initiatives that create financial, strategic, or reputational value for the School.
b) Student Opportunity - This refers to contribution to student-facing practice development, including recruitment support, employability, internship placement, professional mentoring, company visits, live projects, guest speakers, professional certification opportunities, career-facing learning activities, or other structured opportunities that connect students with practice.
c) Practice Impact - This refers to contribution to the School s practice-based knowledge, professional reputation, and external visibility. This may include teaching cases, business intelligence outputs, policy or industry reports, professional publications, media engagement, public-facing expertise, contribution to professional debates, or other forms of knowledge transfer and practice leadership.
In addition, Professors are also expected to hold leadership roles (service) with the Department, School, or the University, using their experience and expertise to represent the Department and the School.
In terms of teaching, all faculty within the Department should be willing and able to teach at all levels, including undergraduate and master's programmes as well as executive education.
QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCES
Essential Qualifications/Experience
Successful applicants to the position are expected to have:
At least 7-year working experience in the industry/institution such as NGO, Think Tanks, government, central bank or other policy/professional institutions
A proven record of making measurable impact on policy or industry practice, evidence of direct value creation, meaningful external engagement
A good personal network with industry and/or government
Adaptability in working in a collegial environment
Desirable Qualifications/Experience
Expertise in the areas of AI-related industry and pharmaceutical industry
A master s degree in management or a related field
Teaching experience in higher education
For Professor level, the successful candidates to the position are expected to also have:
Leadership experience in building or strengthening external relationships, revenue channels, client portfolios, strategic partnerships, or business-facing platforms
Evidence of past contribution has created sustained financial, strategic, or reputational value for the institutions
Well-recognised practice impact, senior professional standing, external visibility, or contribution to professional debates
A sustained record of influential outputs such as business intelligence reports, policy or industry reports, public-facing expertise
CAREER DEVELOPMENT
Clear career development path with annual review.
Professional development trainings are provided.
COMPENSATION & BENEFITS
Salary: Competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Benefits
Allowance: XJTLU provide various month/annual/one-off allowances as
Housing allowance
Travel allowance
Relocation allowance
Etc.
Commercial insurance: international insurance plans customized for XJTLU staff and family members. (details refer to the University Policy)
Paid holidays:
Statutory Holidays (13 days)
Annual Leave (34 days per academic year including university close days and annual leave) )
Family Matters Leave
Paid Sick Leave
Marriage Leave
Paternity Leave
Parental leave
Etc.
Working visa and residence permit in China:
XJTLU sponsors working visa and residence permit in China for the staff.
HOW TO APPLY
Please submit your application on our university website. Applications must be submitted in a single pdf file that includes 3 parts in the order of:
A cover letter
A current CV, including date of birth, country of citizenship, and highest degree level
Contact Details for Three References
For specific enquiries relating to the positions, please contact Dr Jie Li, Head of the Department of Strategic Management and Organisations, at Jie.Li02@xjtlu.edu.cn. Informal enquiries may also be addressed to Ms Yu Yan, HRBP of IBSS, at Yu.Yan@xjtlu.edu.cn. Please quote the position title and job ID in your enquiry.

The Department of Strategic Management and Organisations encompasses the fields of Strategy, International Business, Human Resource Management, Organisational Behaviour and Leadership. The Department actively pursues excellence in student learning and teaching, academic research and social impact, and promotes student-centred education by connecting theory with practice.
Our faculty and PhD students form a diverse and internationally oriented academic community. Members of the Department publish in leading international journals, including Academy of Management Journal, Strategic Management Journal, Journal of International Business Studies, Journal of Applied Psychology, Journal of Management Studies, Organization Studies, Human Resource Management, Journal of Organizational Behavior, Journal of Vocational Behavior, and Journal of World Business.
Members of the Department teach a large number of undergraduate students in Business Administration, International Business with a Language, and Human Resource Management and People Analytics programmes as well as postgraduate students enrolled in the MSc Management or the IMBA programmes.
ABOUT THE POSITION
We are seeking outstanding, internationally engaged and research-active scholars whose research and teaching contribute to the broad and evolving field of management. While we welcome applicants with expertise in all areas of management, we are particularly interested in candidates specialising in one or more of the following priority areas:
Strategy
International Business
Artificial Intelligence in Management
Data-Driven Decision-Making
Digital Transformation
Organisational Change
As these are Research Track appointments, research excellence and the development of an internationally recognised research profile are central to the roles. Successful candidates will be expected to develop ambitious research programmes, publish in high-quality international journals, seek external research funding and contribute to the Department s research culture. They will also deliver high-quality undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, supervise student research and contribute to academic service and citizenship.
Research performance at IBSS is benchmarked against internationally recognised journal-quality guides, including the Academic Journal Guide (ABS) and the ABDC list, with target outputs typically at ABS 3/ABDC A or above. Where appropriate, candidates are also encouraged to develop applied research relevant to the School s industry partnerships and networks. The level of appointment will be determined according to each candidate s qualifications, research record and pipeline, teaching experience, external funding, doctoral supervision, academic leadership and wider contribution to the academic community.
EXPECTATIONS BY LEVEL OF APPOINTMENT
All candidates should demonstrate international experience through their academic career, research collaborations, teaching, professional engagement or other relevant activities. As teaching and academic activities are conducted in English, candidates must demonstrate a high level of English proficiency, including the ability to communicate complex ideas clearly and effectively.
Assistant Professor
We are seeking high-potential, early-career scholars who are developing strong and internationally oriented research profiles.
Candidates should:
Hold a PhD in Management or a closely related discipline, or be close to completion;
Demonstrate a strong research pipeline with clear potential for publication in leading international journals;
Show the capacity to develop an independent and internationally recognised research programme;
Demonstrate the ability to contribute to high-quality teaching in one or more areas of the Department s portfolio;
Show an interest in innovative, research-informed teaching and pedagogy;
Demonstrate the potential to contribute to research, teaching and academic citizenship activities.
Associate Professor
In addition to the expectations for Assistant Professor, candidates should normally demonstrate:
A strong and sustained record of high-quality publications in internationally recognised journals;
A substantial research pipeline demonstrating continued potential for research excellence;
A track record of securing external research funding, preferably including experience as Principal Investigator or leader of externally funded projects;
A strong record of high-quality teaching and innovative pedagogy;
Experience contributing to curriculum development and programme enhancement;
Experience of PhD supervision, with successful doctoral completions desirable;
Evidence of academic leadership, international collaboration and contribution to the Department, School or wider academic community.
Senior Associate Professor
In addition to the expectations for Associate Professor, candidates should demonstrate:
Established international recognition and a substantial, continuing research pipeline;
A strong track record of securing external research funding as Principal Investigator, including significant projects where appropriate;
A sustained record of successful PhD supervision and doctoral completions;
Significant experience of academic leadership and major service or administrative responsibilities;
Meaningful contributions to the wider academic community through activities such as editorial service, scholarly associations, conference leadership or international research networks;
Demonstrated ability to mentor colleagues, develop research capacity and contribute strategically to the discipline s future direction.
Professor
In addition to the expectations for Senior Associate Professor, candidates should demonstrate:
A distinguished and sustained record of research excellence and international scholarly leadership;
A substantial record of publications in leading international journals and an ongoing programme of high-impact research;
A significant record of securing major external research funding and developing internationally recognised research initiatives;
Extensive experience of successful doctoral supervision and the development of early-career researchers;
A strong record of academic leadership, including the ability to shape research, teaching or institutional strategy;
Evidence of mentoring junior faculty and making substantial contributions to the School, University and wider academic or professional communities.

Professional development trainings are provided.

jobs.title: Research Associate - Open Rank
jobs.description:
Job Details
Overview
POSITION SUMMARY:
Under the direction of the Principal Investigator (PI) or designee, the Research Associate provides operational support to the laboratory. The Research Associate will perform research experiments as defined by the PI.
This is an open-rank posting (there are 4 levels of Research Associate) - candidates will be hired into the level commensurate with their experience.
UMass Chan has an immediate opening for a Research Assistant in the Flow Cytometry Core Facility. The right candidate will join a highly experienced team of scientists readily available to share their expertise. The primary duty of the Research Assistant is to provide high-quality flow-cytometry services to support investigators in the UMMS research community on a wide variety of exciting research projects. High people/social skills including listening, teaching & communication are preferred. Fluency in verbal and written English is required. Good problem-solving and organizational skills as well as hands-on, mechanical aptitude with a “can do” attitude are preferred. Candidates should be comfortable working both independently and as part of a team.

Position Summary
The Department of Communication Studies in the College of Communication & Information Sciences at the University of Alabama invites applications for a tenured Associate/Full endowed professorship specializing in interpersonal communication to begin August 16, 2027.
Detailed Position Information
The Robinson Endowed Professor in Interpersonal Communication will contribute to the UA vision as a future-ready flagship by developing leaders and the workforce of the future, advancing research and innovation that address real-world problems, and strengthening communities across Alabama and beyond. More specifically, this position offers elite scholars the resources necessary to develop innovative theoretical/methodological approaches to meaningfully address communication challenges within personal, social, or public contexts. The Robinson Professor will have access to multiple college research labs, work with an award-winning community of multi-disciplinary peers, and lead graduate students to magnify the insights of interpersonal communication scholarship.
The department embraces the full power of communication by studying theory, method, and practice in the areas of interpersonal communication, rhetoric and political discourse, communication and culture, and organizational leadership. We are committed to cultivating responsible, informed, and civically minded students who will be future leaders in their communities and workplaces.
We seek a distinguished scholar with an established record of excellence in research, intellectual leadership, and graduate student mentorship. Expertise in interpersonal communication may include, but are not limited to, the following contexts:
• Small group/team communication
• Technology-mediated relationships
• Political identity and conflict
• Intercultural communication and collaboration
• Family communication
• Trust, deception, and authenticity
• Health communication
Tenured faculty teaching assignments may include undergraduate, master's-level, as well as contributions or course assignments within the interdisciplinary doctoral program. The Robinson Family endowment provides this position with funds to accelerate research and professional development, including a reduced teaching load and/or summer research support.
Minimum Qualifications
• A PhD in Communication or a closely related field.
• Strong expertise in the area of interpersonal communication.
• National reputation as a leading interpersonal communication scholar.
Preferred Qualifications
• Demonstrable expertise with external funding. • Evidence of effective graduate student mentorship. • Successful design and delivery of relevant courses. • Adept at interdisciplinary collaboration.
Instructions and Required Materials for Application
To apply, provide the following: 1. Cover letter highlighting connection to the position with explicit discussion of program of research, excellence in mentorship and teaching, and potential for extramural funding. 2. Curriculum vitae. 3. Names and contact information for three references who will be contacted during the campus interview phase of this search. The search committee will begin reviewing applications on December 1, 2027 and review of applications will continue until the position is filled. Questions regarding the search should be directed to the search chair, Dr. Robin Boylorn (rboylorn@ua.edu)
About the Division/College/School
The College of Communication & Information Sciences has four academic units, approximately 110 full-time faculty members, and serves approximately 3,500 students across bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degree programs, including approximately 95 students in the college-wide Ph.D. program. The college’s Institute for Communication & Information Research (ICIR) is a premier research institute dedicated to addressing societal and cultural issues related to communication and information research. The ICIR collaborates with businesses, nonprofit organizations, government agencies, foundations, and other entities to produce high-impact research that informs and improves our evolving communication and information landscape. The College is also home to the Public Opinion Lab, equipped with the Sprinklr data warehouse and custom data collection and management resources; a biometrics lab outfitted with state-of-the-art iMotions software and associated hardware; and the near-term development of an interactive VR/theater lab, among others. The college is also home to the Holle Center for Communication Arts, whose mission is guided by a commitment to advance narrative justice through innovative and arts-informed research, community engagement, and creative co-operation. The college also maintains the 40,000 square-foot Digital Media Center, which is home to Alabama Public Radio and WVUA 23, a full-power commercial television station serving a top-50 television market.
About the Department of Communication Studies
The department consists of 26 full-time faculty members dedicated to furthering the education of nearly 1,000 undergraduate majors and minors, and over 100 online and on-campus graduate students. Our department is also home to a renowned forensics program and a cutting-edge Speaking Studio. The department actively participates in the college’s interdisciplinary PhD program.
The department is a collaborative environment that values the communication discipline’s rich heritage of methodological diversity. Our team is committed to creating belonging through valuing diverse viewpoints and cultures. For more information, visit our website at https://comstudies.ua.edu.
About the University
The University of Alabama is located in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, named one of Travel + Leisure’s 25 Best College Towns and Cities in the U.S. As one of the nation’s premier universities, UA offers bachelor’s, master's and doctoral degrees in nearly 200 fields of study. With more than 1,400 acres of tree-lined academic core campus and over 300 state-of-the art facilities, UA has been ranked among the most beautiful and most impressive college campuses in the South, in the state of Alabama and in the nation.
In Fall 2023, the Capstone set a new enrollment record with more than 39,000 students, including more than 8,200 in the freshman class. The current enrollment includes students from every county in Alabama, every state in the nation and 92 countries around the world. More than 1,100 National Merit Scholars are currently enrolled, making UA one of the largest enrolling institutions of the scholars in the country.
UA was recently recognized as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. students for the seventh time in nine years, as well as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. Scholars for the first time. UA is one of only 12 universities in the nation to receive both honors.
For reasons like this, the University made Forbes list of America’s Top Colleges for 2023 and Time magazine’s list of Top 50 Best Colleges for Future Leaders. It also made Princeton Review’s list of Top Value Colleges.
UA is also designated among the top doctoral research universities in the United States in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. One of the fastest growing major research institutions in the nation, UA saw a 21% increase in sponsored awards in the 2023 fiscal year.
Since 2015, UA has invested over $1.1 billion in the physical campus, adding more than 2.55 million gross square feet of space, over 150 new research-intensive faculty, signature research areas (e.g., “The Alabama Research Institutes”), and a growing number of partnerships with industry and with state and federal agencies.
The University employs nearly 2,100 faculty and over 4,500 staff, with 52 UA researchers included in the National Academy of Inventors. An additional 40 current faculty have received the NSF CAREER Award, the nation’s most prestigious recognition of top performing young scientists in disciplines ranging from nanoscience and engineering to biological sciences.

jobs.title: Faculty Position (Assistant or Associate Professor) in Large Animal Anesthesia
jobs.description:
Job Details
Faculty Position (Assistant or Associate Professor) in Large Animal Anesthesia
Location: Kennett Square, PA
Open Date: Oct 30, 2026
Deadline:
The Department of Clinical Studies-New Bolton Center at the University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine (Penn Vet) invites applications for a faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor level in large animal anesthesia, with a focus on equine anesthesia. The position will be in the Associated Faculty in the Academic Clinician (AC) track, which focuses on clinical service and teaching. A typical division of effort for faculty in the AC track at New Bolton Center is 90% time on clinics, including clinical service and clinical teaching, and 10% time off clinics for academic efforts. Didactic and laboratory teaching and administrative or other service duties are included in both on- and off-clinic time.
Applications are also being accepted for the position in our Clinician-Educator track, which carries with it assigned time and expectations for research or other scholarly productivity. Please see position number ***** for further details on the position as Clinician Educator. A total of two positions will be filled.
This position offers the opportunity to join a team of passionate clinical and didactic educators with a shared commitment to excellence in patient care and a significant emphasis on teaching in the clinical environment. The Section of Anesthesia is home to four diplomates of the American or European Colleges of Veterinary Anesthesia and Analgesia and to three anesthesia technicians. Five residents in training for ACVAA/ECVAA board certification divide their time between Penn Vet's Matthew J. Ryan Veterinary Hospital for Companion Animals and the New Bolton Center Hospital, while an additional clinical fellow is dedicated full-time to New Bolton Center.
Clinical service and clinical teaching are at the heart of this position. The New Bolton Center Hospital for Large Animals provides an exceptional environment for both, with approximately 1,400 animals anesthetized each year for a wide variety of procedures. Clinical responsibilities include primary anesthesia care, pain management, supervision and mentorship of technicians and residents in the anesthetic management of patients (the majority of which are equine), as well as participation in the after-hours anesthesia rotation. Clinical effort is based at the New Bolton Center Hospital; however, faculty who are interested may also have opportunities to participate in the clinical services at the Ryan Veterinary Hospital as well as in delivery of anesthesia at zoos and animal parks in the surrounding area.
The Department of Clinical Studies-New Bolton Center includes more than 40 diplomates of American and European specialty colleges, including 15 faculty who are double-boarded, providing opportunities for interaction across a broad range of specialties. The faculty share a strong commitment to collaborative, compassionate patient care. The multidisciplinary environment provides frequent opportunities for case discussion and exchange of perspectives across specialties, including through morbidity and mortality rounds, grand rounds, clinical ethics discussions, and informal consultation on the clinical floor. Anesthesiologists are valued contributors to these discussions and to patient care throughout the hospital.
Teaching is integrated throughout the clinical program and provides opportunities to work closely with veterinary students, interns, residents, technicians, and colleagues. In addition to case-based teaching on the clinical floor, faculty contribute to didactic and laboratory instruction and other educational activities. The position is particularly well-suited to an individual who enjoys teaching in the context of clinical practice, values mentorship and the exchange of ideas, and would welcome the opportunity to help learners develop their knowledge, technical skills, clinical reasoning, and confidence. Penn Vet students and house officers are highly qualified, motivated, and eager to learn, and faculty share a strong commitment to creating a supportive and engaging educational experience.
Research is not a requirement of this position; however, faculty in the AC track who have an interest in scholarly activity are welcome to participate in collaborative projects, including clinical research, study design, enrollment of clinical cases in research trials, and manuscript preparation. New Bolton Center's active research community provides opportunities for involvement at a level that complements each faculty member's clinical and educational interests.
The successful candidate has the potential to access the clinical, teaching, and research units on the campus, including the Veterinary School's 200-cow Marshak Dairy and the 250-sow Penn Swine Teaching & Research Center. The Advanced Imaging and Translational Center, currently in the pre-construction phase, will provide state-of-the-art imaging modalities such as 3T MRI, multi-axis mobile-gantry CT, and intra-operative CT. Opportunities exist for interaction and collaboration with other initiatives and departments, including the Center for Stewardship Agriculture and Food Security, Pathobiology, Wildlife Futures, and core laboratories.
Located in the heart of Chester County's horse country, Kennett Square offers an appealing blend of rural beauty and small-town charm. The area's rich equestrian tradition, farms, and vibrant community create opportunities to pursue interests outside of work, from riding and local competitions to exploring the scenic countryside. A welcoming downtown with restaurants and shops, along with convenient access to Philadelphia and Wilmington, makes Kennett Square a rewarding place to live and build a career.
Qualifications
Requirements include a DVM/VMD or equivalent degree, and board certification or eligibility in either the ACVAA or ECVAA. Salary and rank will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Application Instructions

jobs.description:
Job Details
Faculty Position (Assistant or Associate Professor) in Large Animal Anesthesia
Location: Kennett Square, PA
Open Date: Oct 30, 2026
Deadline:
The Department of Clinical Studies-New Bolton Center at the University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine (Penn Vet) invites applications for a faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor level in large animal anesthesia, with a focus on equine anesthesia. The position will be in the Standing Faculty in the Clinician-Educator (CE) track, which supports faculty members whose responsibilities include the traditional triad of clinical service, teaching, and research. A typical division of effort for faculty in the CE track at New Bolton Center is 70% time on clinics, including clinical service and clinical teaching, and 30% time off clinics for academic efforts, including independent or collaborative research and other scholarly activity. Didactic and laboratory teaching and administrative or other service duties are included in both on- and off-clinic time. The division of effort can be modified according to the focus of the successful candidate.
Applications are also being accepted for the position in our Academic Clinician track, which focuses on clinical service and teaching and has no research requirement. Please see position number ***** for further details on the position as Academic Clinician. A total of two positions will be filled.
This position offers the opportunity to join a team of passionate clinical and didactic educators with a shared commitment to excellence in patient care and a significant emphasis on teaching in the clinical environment. The successful candidate will contribute to the clinical, teaching, and research missions of the Section of Anesthesia at New Bolton Center. The Section is home to four diplomates of the American or European Colleges of Veterinary Anesthesia and Analgesia, and to three anesthesia technicians. Five residents in training for ACVAA/ECVAA board certification divide their time between Penn Vet's Matthew J. Ryan Veterinary Hospital for Companion Animals and the New Bolton Center Hospital, while an additional clinical fellow is dedicated full-time to New Bolton Center.
The New Bolton Center Hospital for Large Animals provides an exceptional environment for both clinical service and clinical teaching, with approximately 1,400 animals anesthetized each year for a wide variety of procedures. Clinical responsibilities include primary anesthesia care, pain management, supervision and mentorship of technicians and residents in the anesthetic management of patients (the majority of which are equine), as well as participation in the after-hours anesthesia rotation. Clinical effort is based at the New Bolton Center Hospital; however, faculty who are interested may also have opportunities to participate in the clinical services at the Ryan Veterinary Hospital as well as in delivery of anesthesia at zoos and animal parks in the surrounding area.
The Department of Clinical Studies-New Bolton Center includes more than 40 diplomates of American and European specialty colleges, including 15 faculty who are double-boarded, providing opportunities for interaction across a broad range of specialties. The faculty share a strong commitment to collaborative, compassionate patient care. The multidisciplinary environment provides frequent opportunities for case discussion and exchange of perspectives across specialties, including through morbidity and mortality rounds, grand rounds, clinical ethics discussions, and informal consultation on the clinical floor. Anesthesiologists are valued contributors to these discussions and to patient care throughout the hospital.
Teaching is integrated throughout the clinical program and provides opportunities to work closely with veterinary students, interns, residents, technicians, and colleagues. In addition to case-based teaching on the clinical floor, faculty contribute to didactic and laboratory instruction and other educational activities. The position is well-suited to an individual who enjoys teaching in the context of clinical practice, values mentorship and the exchange of ideas, and would welcome the opportunity to help learners develop their knowledge, technical skills, clinical reasoning, and confidence. Penn Vet students and house officers are highly qualified, motivated, and eager to learn, and faculty share a strong commitment to creating a supportive and engaging educational experience.
Research and scholarly activity are an integral part of the CE track, with dedicated off-clinic time provided to support these efforts. The 27 Clinician-Educators and 10 tenure-track faculty perform the majority of the Department's research, along with post-veterinary residency students enrolled in studies toward the PhD degree in the University of Pennsylvania's Biomedical Graduate Studies through funding by New Bolton Center's Penn Veterinary Scientist Training program, and post-doctoral trainees, fellows and visiting scholars. The Section of Anesthesia supports an active and growing research program, focused on cardiovascular and respiratory physiology and pathophysiology, advanced pain management and pharmacology. Candidates are encouraged to pursue scholarly activities in areas relevant to their interests and expertise. A rich collaborative environment provides opportunities for interdisciplinary research within Penn Vet and the broader University of Pennsylvania community, as well as with veterinary institutions, medical schools, and industry partners nationally and internationally.
The successful candidate has the potential to access the clinical, teaching, and research units on the campus, including the Veterinary School's 200-cow Marshak Dairy and the 250-sow Penn Swine Teaching & Research Center. The Advanced Imaging and Translational Center, currently in the pre-construction phase, will provide state-of-the-art imaging modalities such as 3T MRI, multi-axis mobile-gantry CT, and intra-operative CT. Opportunities exist for interaction and collaboration with other initiatives and departments, including the Center for Stewardship Agriculture and Food Security, Pathobiology, Wildlife Futures, and core laboratories working on microbial genomics, stem cell biology, orthopedic disease, and germ cell biology on the New Bolton Center Campus, and numerous programs in Philadelphia's lively University District. The three other departments of Penn Vet are located at the center of Philadelphia's interactive biomedical research environment, in close proximity to the Perelman School of Medicine, the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, Penn Dental Medicine, The Wistar Institute, and a vast array of core facilities.
Located in the heart of Chester County's horse country, Kennett Square offers an appealing blend of rural beauty and small-town charm. The area's rich equestrian tradition, farms, and vibrant community create opportunities to pursue interests outside of work, from riding and local competitions to exploring the scenic countryside. A welcoming downtown with restaurants and shops, along with convenient access to Philadelphia and Wilmington, makes Kennett Square a rewarding place to live and build a career.
Qualifications
Requirements include a DVM/VMD or equivalent degree, board certification or eligibility in either the ACVAA or ECVAA, and evidence of research or other scholarly activity, preferably in areas relevant to anesthesia. Salary and rank will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Application Instructions
Application review will begin immediately, and applications will be considered until the positions are filled. Questions about the position can be directed to Dr. Billy I. Smith, Search Committee Chair, by email at bis@vet.upenn.edu.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Clinical Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice, Acute Care
Job Description Summary, Duties and Responsibilities, Required Qualifications and Preferred Qualifications
The search will remain open until the position is filled. For full consideration, applications should be submitted by January 15, 2027. Applications received after this date may be reviewed at the discretion of the search committee.
________________________________________________________________________________________________________
The University of Rhode Island is the state's flagship land and sea-grant research institution, with a commitment to urban initiatives. A student-centered research institution, URI actively partners with other organizations globally and locally to advance knowledge and to develop informed residents and leaders. URI is committed to community engagement, excellence in education, and solving the world's most important challenges. Situated on the traditional land and territories of the Narragansett Nation and the Niantic People along the Atlantic Ocean, URI strives to create a diverse and inclusive environment for researchers, teachers, learners, and community members.
The College of Pharmacy is on the main campus in Washington County, Rhode Island. Washington County is Rhode Island's southernmost region, covering 100 miles of coastline and sandy beaches along the Atlantic Ocean. The College of Pharmacy is a welcoming and inclusive community of scholars with a vision to "Advance Health and Transform Communities." The College community seeks to pursue lives of service and intellectual exploration to solve scientific challenges and deliver progressive interdisciplinary healthcare with compassion and intention.
The Department of Pharmacy Practice and Clinical Research prepares outstanding and compassionate pharmacists and health outcomes specialists who excel as clinicians, scholars, and leaders. We aim to strengthen and diversify the practice of pharmacy. We seek a Clinical Assistant Professor of Pharmacy committed to expanding our community of scholars who work together and inspire one another in teaching, research, practice, and service.
We seek applicants who are committed to embodying the College's values. We are a people-first community that is inclusive, accessible, equitable, and diverse, and that respects the rights and dignity of all individuals. We support the physical and mental well-being of our community and value the freedom to learn, teach, conduct research, and disseminate knowledge in service of the public good. We promote integrity and innovation through lifelong learning, ethical practice, research, and leadership. We also value excellence in service, ongoing reflection, and shared accountability as we work to strengthen the URI community and serve Rhode Island and the broader world.
The University of Rhode Island College of Pharmacy values and respects all individuals. We are committed to recruiting and retaining a values-driven workforce to enhance our student environment and the health of all people in Rhode Island, the United States, and the world. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who demonstrate through their efforts in teaching, research, and engagement that create environments to promote belonging in education and support health accessibility to improve outcomes.
POSITION SUMMARY:
The University of Rhode Island College of Pharmacy invites applications for a full-time, calendar-year, non-tenure-track Clinical Assistant Professor in Pharmacy Practice, specializing in acute care pharmacy. This shared academic-clinical position includes approximately 32 hours per week dedicated to College of Pharmacy responsibilities and 8 hours per week embedded at the clinical practice site as an integrated member of the pharmacy team. This three-year appointment, housed in the Department of Pharmacy Practice and Clinical Research, includes responsibilities for clinical teaching, service, and scholarly activity. Continuation beyond the initial term is expected based on successful performance review. Salary is commensurate with qualifications and experience and includes a comprehensive benefits package. The selected candidate will be expected to develop an exemplary clinical practice model, demonstrate excellence in both didactic and experiential teaching, provide meaningful service to the profession, the college, and the university, and contribute to clinically relevant scholarship.
KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Contribute to the Doctor of Pharmacy and graduate teaching missions of the University by mentoring and teaching graduate, professional degree, and undergraduate required and elective courses for the College.
• Establish and maintain a high-quality experiential training site at a partnering healthcare institution by developing an exemplary clinical practice model focused on acute care pharmacy.
• This will involve close collaboration with the clinical site, the Director of Experiential Education, and the Chair of the Department of Pharmacy Practice and Clinical Research to support advanced pharmacy practice experiences (APPE) and interprofessional education.
• Teach in didactic and experiential components of the Doctor of Pharmacy curriculum, including core and elective courses related to acute care and pharmacotherapy.
• Engage in sustained scholarly activity, including peer-reviewed publications and presentations at regional, national, or international professional meetings.
• Work collaboratively with patients and their families, pharmacists, nurses, residents, faculty, physicians, and other health professionals.
• Actively contribute to curriculum development and assessment aligned with accreditation standards and participate in service through committee involvement at both the College and University levels.
OTHER DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Perform other duties as assigned.
ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS:
The incumbent is not substantially exposed to adverse environmental conditions.
QUALIFICATIONS
REQUIRED:
1. Doctor of Pharmacy degree from an ACPE-accredited college or university.
2. Licensed or eligible for pharmacist licensure in Rhode Island.
3. Completion of PGY1 or PGY2 pharmacy residency training or equivalent clinical experience, generally demonstrated by a minimum of five years of acute care pharmacy practice.
4. Demonstrated clinical expertise in acute care pharmacy practice.
5. Eligibility to obtain or achieve board certification in pharmacy specialties (e.g. BCPS).
6. Demonstrated strong interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills.
PREFERRED:
1. Evidence of effective didactic, experiential, or interprofessional teaching.
2. Experience precepting student pharmacists and/or pharmacy residents.
3. Evidence of scholarly productivity or the potential to establish a sustained program of scholarship.
4. Ability to contribute to teaching across a broad range of acute care and pharmacotherapy topics.
5. Experience collaborating within interprofessional healthcare teams.
6. Demonstrated ability to foster an inclusive and accessible learning and clinical environment that supports the success of individuals from varied backgrounds.
______________________________________________________________________________________________________

jobs.description:
Job Details
The School of Art at the University of Arkansas invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Graphic Design to start August 2027. This is a standard nine-month faculty appointment with a workload of 40% teaching, 40% research/creative activity, and 20% service. Teaching will be the equivalent of a 2/2 load in the Graphic Design BFA program, the Master of Design in Communication Design, the upcoming design minor, and/or the school’s foundations program. The ideal candidate brings practical knowledge in emerging technologies and design futures, including areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, virtual reality, augmented reality, extended reality, experimental design, data visualization, speculative design, and other innovative design methods. The successful candidate will demonstrate future-thinking mindsets in teaching, creative practice, and scholarly research, with consideration for how AI is transforming visual communication, design authorship, image-making, typography, branding, interaction, publishing, and other areas of graphic-design practice.
This is an in-person position, not a remote position. Most university classes are offered face-to-face, and extensive in-person engagement in such activities as office hours, student advising, and departmental, college, and university committee meetings is essential to advancing student success and departmental effectiveness.
Regular, reliable, and non-disruptive attendance is an essential job duty, as is the ability to create and maintain collegial, harmonious working relationships with others.
About the School of Art:
Housed in the Fulbright College of Arts and Sciences, the University of Arkansas School of Art offers undergraduate degrees and tuition-free graduate programs in art education, art history, graphic design and studio art, including ceramics, drawing, painting, photography, printmaking and sculpture. Formerly the Department of Art, the School of Art was established in 2017 following a transformative $120 million gift from the Walton Family Charitable Support Foundation. With additional support from the Windgate Foundation, the School of Art developed the Windgate Art + Design District, providing state-of-the-art facilities and strong partnerships with regional arts institutions. Learn more at art.uark.edu.
About the Graphic Design Program:
With 110 undergraduate students, 14 graduate students, and 9 full-time faculty, we are a vibrant community of creatives who are passionate about designing at the edge of what is possible and what is preferable for the future of communities, culture, and technology. Housed in the brand-new Studio + Design Center, the Graphic Design program’s facilities include large studio classroom spaces, multiple state-of-the-art technology and equipment labs, risograph and letterpress printers, and a special projects Design Clinic.
Minimum Qualifications:
Terminal degree (PhD, MFA, MDes, MGD) in Graphic Design (or a closely related field such as visual communication) from an accredited institution of higher education conferred by the first date of appointment
At least one academic year of university-level teaching experience as a graduate teaching assistant with classroom teaching responsibilities or instructor of record in graphic design or a closely related field
Evidence of an active research agenda and/or scholarly/creative activity in emerging technologies
Preferred Qualifications:
Two or more years of university-level teaching experience as instructor of record in graphic design or a closely related field
Demonstrated experience in interdisciplinary, transdisciplinary, and/or cross-campus collaborations
Demonstrated research trajectory related to emerging technologies such as VR/AR, artificial intelligence, data visualization
Experience in mentoring undergraduate and graduate students and design program coordination
Evidence of strong interpersonal communication as demonstrated in applicant materials
Salary Information:
Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Cover Letter/Letter of Application, Curriculum Vitae, List of three Professional References (name, email, business title), Other (see special instructions for details), Statement of Teaching Philosophy

Job Details:
The E. Craig Wall Sr. Wall College of Business Administration at Coastal Carolina University invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track position at the assistant or associate professor level in Hospitality, Resort, and Tourism Management (HRTM) in, beginning Fall 2027. The Department of Marketing and Hospitality, Resort, and Tourism Management seeks an innovative, student-centered faculty member who will contribute to excellence in teaching, scholarship, and service. Candidates should hold a Ph.D. or D.B.A. in hospitality management, tourism management, hotel or resort management, or a closely related discipline from an accredited institution. A.B.D. candidates with a clear plan for degree completion by August 2027 may be considered. Candidates must demonstrate an active or developing research agenda with the potential for meaningful scholarly impact in the hospitality and tourism discipline, along with a commitment to teaching excellence and student-centered instruction. Rank will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. The department is especially interested in candidates prepared to teach in areas such as hospitality operations, resort management, event management, tourism, revenue management, hospitality marketing, sustainability, analytics, or technology. The ideal candidate would also bring some combination of professional experience or credentials in the hospitality, tourism, or broader service industries; a record of experiential and applied teaching, and industry engagement that can support student projects, applied research, and/or external funding. The teaching load is typically three courses per semester and may include face-to-face, hybrid, and/or online delivery. In addition to teaching, the successful candidate will be expected to develop engaging and industry-responsive curricula; mentor students; maintain an active research agenda that results in quality publications; and contribute to departmental, college, university, professional, and community service activities. The successful candidate will also build relationships with industry partners and bring industry engagement, applied learning, and professional development into the educational experience.
Accredited by AACSB International, the Wall College of Business serves more than 3,000 graduate and undergraduate students. The college offers undergraduate majors in seven disciplines (Accounting, Commercial and Investment Real Estate Economics, Finance, Management, Marketing, Hospitality and Tourism Management), as well as MBA and M.S. in Finance graduate programs. Classification Minimum Requirements:

Eight years of relevant professional experience, including a record of progressive scholarly accomplishment. At least three years of leadership and supervisory responsibility in a research library, with demonstrated experience leading change and fostering professional development and growth.

Job Description:
The George A. Smathers Libraries, University of Florida, seeks applications and nominations for the position of Department Chair for Special and Area Studies Collections. The successful candidate will be accomplished and forward-thinking, and enthusiastic about leading special and area studies in a new era for the UF libraries. Reporting to the Associate Dean, this position is a key member of the library team, heading a department comprising some of the libraries' most distinctive and internationally significant collections.
The Chair of the Department of Special and Area Studies Collections (SASC) is a year-round (12 month) tenure track library faculty position, based in the historic Smathers Library. This position will provide leadership, strategic vision and direction for the department to expand collections and usage, increase available resources, manage spaces, advocate for facility improvements, and strengthen the department's capacity to preserve and provide access to its collections. The Chair works collaboratively with departmental colleagues to assess strengths and weaknesses in the fourteen collections, determine priorities, establish policies, and develop departmental service plans that enhance and support the academic mission of the University. The Chair of the Department of Special and Area Studies Collections (SASC) will pursue professional development opportunities, including research, publication, and professional service activities to meet library-wide criteria for tenure and promotion.
For a candidate ready to assume a major leadership role, this position offers the opportunity to guide internationally significant collections while advancing research, teaching, public engagement, and the long-term stewardship of cultural heritage. The libraries seek candidates who demonstrate curiosity, dedication, and a collaborative spirit in working with the campus community to foster engagement with special and area studies collections.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Collaborates with the Dean of University Libraries and the Associate Dean to devise and implement strategies to achieve goals relating to the education, research, and outreach mission of the department.
Works with departmental faculty and staff to define needs, set priorities, develop policies, and establish goals, objectives, strategic plans, and budgets to ensure effective management and development of services and collections.
Partners with the Dean of University Libraries, the Associate Dean and the Director of Advancement, to seek financial support for the department's collections and operations.
Oversees and coordinates the work of the units comprising the department of approximately 30 faculty and staff.
Coordinates with collection managers and communicates work to the Libraries' Administration.
With department faculty and staff, oversees public facing events that showcase and enhance the curricular and scholarly use of the University of Florida's Special and Area Studies Collections within the academic and research communities.
Fosters a collaborative work environment, encouraging personnel to work within and across departments in the University Libraries and other units across campus to support the goals and initiatives of the Libraries' strategic plan.
Participates actively in the cooperative management of the Libraries through service on the Joint Chairs group, Branch Chairs, and other library consultative bodies. Participates in University of Florida committees as appropriate.
Represents Special and Area Studies and the George A. Smathers Libraries at the state and national levels, advancing awareness of the Libraries' collections, services, expertise, and public mission.
Pursues professional development goals, including publication and leadership in appropriate professional organizations on the state, regional and national levels to meet the requirements for tenure.
SPECIAL AND AREA STUDIES COLLECTIONS
The Special and Area Studies Collections Department stewards distinctive and internationally recognized collections in support of the academic mission of the University of Florida. Located in the heart of campus, the department supports UF faculty, staff, students, external researchers and the public from within the historic Smathers Library. The department's holdings related to Florida heritage, Latin America and the Caribbean, Anglo-American children's literature, and Judaica are exceptional among academic libraries in North America. Recognized for its innovative approach to stewardship, access, teaching, and public engagement, the department's collections and programs reflect the preeminence of the University of Florida, the institution's land-grant origins, and Florida's unique position as a hemispheric gateway. For more information about the collections, please visit: http://www.uflib.ufl.edu/spec/.
